title: Zhaoyu
author: Wen Xin Yu
synopsis:
The refined yet scheming son of the Grand Princess vs. the sharp-tongued but honest eldest daughter of the Marquis's household.

[Pure Ancient Chinese Setting] [No Time Travel, No Rebirth]

The eldest daughter of the Yongchang Marquis's household, Gao Zhaoyu, has been betrothed to the second son of the prestigious Cui family, Cui Yan, since childhood. The wedding date was all that remained to be set.

Gao Zhaoyu had assumed there would be no further complications with the marriage, but just as the two families were finalizing the arrangements, Cui Yan was caught in bed with his cousin...

Gao Zhaoyu: "In that case, let's call off this marriage."

But the eldest son, Cui Heng, smiled warmly and said, "A union between two families cannot be abandoned. Since that is the case, I will marry Zhaoyu."

chapters.title: Caught in the Act
chapters.content:
"Mmm... Yan Lang... be gentler..."

A coquettish woman, seemingly unable to restrain herself, moaned softly. Her face was flushed with desire as she clung to the man above her, her neck arching unpredictably, her eyes half-lidded and alluring.

The man was none other than Cui Yan, the legitimate second son of the Cui family. His brows were tightly knit, his entire body drenched in sweat. Upon hearing her words, he cursed under his breath and slapped her thigh.

"Ah... stop it~ Yan Lang..." came another round of breathy gasps.

Yongchang Marquis's Mansion, Inner Hall.

"Third Miss is truly gifted with beauty and talent. The first two misses of the Gao family are already engaged, so my unworthy son is unlucky."

Madame Li Zhuangjin, wife of the Yongchang Marquis, sat gracefully, smiling as she accepted the flattery from Madame Liu, wife of the Minister of Rites. Naturally, she was pleased with the praise for her daughters.

Her eldest daughter, Zhaoyu, had been betrothed to the Cui family, the most prestigious clan, seven years ago. Though Cui Yan had chosen an unconventional path by becoming a military officer, which had initially displeased her, now that he had risen to the rank of a sixth-grade official, she could no longer complain. There was nothing to criticize about Zhaoyu's marriage.

The second miss, Yao Jia, born to a secondary wife, had only recently held her coming-of-age ceremony and was also engaged, to the son of the Minister of Personnel.

The only one in the Yongchang Marquis's household who had not yet been betrothed was her youngest daughter, Wen Zhu. Today was the day of her coming-of-age ceremony.

Madame Liu was more than happy to flatter Madame Li. She pretended to chide her: "Oh, Madame, the smile at the corner of your mouth is impossible to hide. Just look at you all."

The surrounding ladies also laughed.

Just as the ladies were filled with laughter, a clear and bright voice preceded its owner into the room: "Mother!"

Gao Wen Zhu walked in smiling and greeted the ladies properly: "Greetings to all the madames!"

Everyone turned to see a girl in a bright red brocade robe with a golden lotus pattern sweeping in like a gust of wind.

Her hair was neatly styled in a hanging bun, adorned with a few delicate pearl flowers, and a small red floral ornament on her forehead, which accentuated her fair, jade-like complexion.

Her face was lit with an unrestrained, radiant smile, her almond-shaped eyes bent into crescents, her gaze clear and bright, full of liveliness.

This was the star of today's coming-of-age ceremony; Gao Wen Zhu, the third miss of the Yongchang Marquis's household.

She walked briskly to her mother, Madame Li Zhuangjin, and performed a proper greeting. As she rose, she playfully winked and whispered:

"Mother, please don't be angry. Just now, I was trying on hairpins in the warming pavilion. That solid gold hibiscus pin was so heavy, my neck ached. I rested a little longer."

Though she spoke softly, her clear voice carried, and the nearby ladies heard her. They immediately covered their mouths, laughing.

Madame Li Zhuangjin found it both amusing and exasperating. She lightly tapped Wen Zhu's forehead: "You naughty monkey, so many madames are waiting for you."

Gao Wen Zhu immediately turned to Madame Liu and the others, greeting them again with poise and a sweet smile: "Wen Zhu was being playful and kept you all waiting. Later, I will serve tea in place of wine to apologize."

Her lively and lovely demeanor made Madame Liu grow fonder of her by the minute. She stepped forward, took Wen Zhu's hand, and said to Madame Li with a smile: "Madame, you said Third Miss is mischievous, but I think her personality is so endearing! She's both well-mannered and lively. This is the spirit a noble lady should have!"

Gao Wen Zhu feigned shyness, lowering her head slightly.

Madame Li Zhuangjin smiled in satisfaction: "Yes, this third daughter of mine may not be as dignified and steady as her eldest sister, and she is a bit unrestrained, but her heart is in the right place."

Madame Liu held onto Gao Wen Zhu's hand, refusing to let go, and laughed heartily: "Oh, Madame, you're being modest. If I had a daughter like this, I'd probably smile in my sleep!"

Madame Li Zhuangjin, pleased by these words, knew what Madame Liu was hinting at but did not respond. Instead, she picked up her teacup and took a sip.

Hu Madame, who was on good terms with Madame Liu, chimed in: "Your eldest son is also outstanding. He managed to enter the Imperial College. In the future, he will surely achieve great things."

Madame Liu immediately smiled modestly: "Oh, no, no. My unworthy son only knows how to bury his head in books. The most important matter in his life hasn't even been settled yet. If he could marry a daughter-in-law like Third Miss, then I would truly have no regrets."

Gao Wen Zhu's face grew redder and redder as she listened. Meanwhile, Madame Li Zhuangjin pretended not to hear, neither rejecting nor accepting, merely smiling faintly as she sipped her tea.

Gao Wen Zhu pretended to stamp her foot in frustration: "Madame Liu. Wen Zhu is still young!"

This action amused everyone once more.

Madame Liu did not press the matter further. She stopped there: "Good child, when you have time in the future, come visit my home. I like your personality."

The matter was thus glossed over.

Though Madame Liu was disappointed, she understood that the status of the Yongchang Marquis's household was not something her family could casually aspire to. If she continued, it might cause everyone to lose face.

Madame Li Zhuangjin finally spoke: "Only you, Madame Liu, appreciate her personality. I, on the other hand, worry about her every day."

Gao Wen Zhu did not want her mother to speak of her in front of so many people. She stepped forward and wrapped her arm around Madame Li Zhuangjin's: "Mother, why hasn't Elder Sister arrived yet?"

Madame Li Zhuangjin smiled sincerely this time: "Old Madame Cui is coming, so I asked your elder sister to go to the front gate to welcome her."

The ladies exchanged glances, understanding the situation.

It seemed the marriage between the Cui and Gao families was about to be finalized. Even the reclusive Old Madame Cui had made an appearance.

Gao Wen Zhu was not surprised. She simply smiled: "Mother, then let's go welcome Old Madame Cui together."

Madame Li Zhuangjin considered this for a moment. Seeing her youngest daughter's suggestion, she agreed. Though she was reluctant to lower her status, Zhaoyu was about to marry into the Cui family, so she had to give Old Madame Cui some face.

Madame Li Zhuangjin, pulled along by her youngest daughter, stood up gracefully and said to the ladies in the hall: "Old Madame Cui's arrival is an honor for our household. I will go welcome her. Please, everyone, remain seated. Enjoy the tea and refreshments, and do not stand on ceremony."

Though Madame Li Zhuangjin spoke politely, the ladies knew they could not remain seated while she went alone. The Madame of Annan County was the first to rise: "I have not seen Old Madame Cui in a long time. How could I let you go alone, Madame?"

The other ladies nodded in agreement. Madame Li Zhuangjin did not refuse. She took Gao Wen Zhu's hand, surrounded by maids and servants, and left the main hall. They walked along the covered corridor toward the second gate.

Gao Wen Zhu leaned against her mother, her steps light, pointing and laughing at the newly bloomed magnolia trees outside the corridor, exuding an air of innocence and liveliness.

As they reached a fork in the path, one direction led to the outer hall beyond the second gate, where the Yongchang Marquis's household received male guests. The other direction led to the rear garden and several quieter courtyards.

Madame Li Zhuangjin was about to head toward the second gate when Gao Wen Zhu suddenly exclaimed, "Huh?" She stopped in her tracks and listened carefully.

"Mother, do you hear... that... isn't there a strange noise?" She pointed toward the path leading to the rear garden, her face filled with confusion.

The following ladies had not yet heard anything, but seeing Gao Wen Zhu pointing toward the rear garden, they leaned in to listen.

From the ear room on the west side of the rear garden came a series of muffled sounds; soft, breathy moans from a woman mixed with a man's low, rough curses. The sounds drifted through the window lattice, falling unpleasantly on the ears within the marquis's courtyard.

Gao Wen Zhu, who was at the front, suddenly stopped. Her hearing was sharp, and the woman's voice, though soft and melodious, sounded vaguely familiar.

Madame Li Zhuangjin's face darkened.

The surrounding ladies gradually caught on, their smiles freezing instantly as they exchanged shocked and suspicious glances. A few of them quickly concealed a flicker of schadenfreude in their eyes.

Madame Li Zhuangjin's face was as dark as water. Today was Wen Zhu's coming-of-age ceremony, and the mansion was filled with guests. How could such vulgar noises come from the ear room in the rear garden? If this spread, wouldn't it become a joke throughout the capital?

Seeing that everyone had heard, she had no choice but to suppress her mounting fury. She signaled the managing nanny to step forward and open the door.

The nanny, being perceptive, approached quietly and asked Madame Li Zhuangjin for confirmation before pushing the door open.

Madame Li Zhuangjin coldly stepped forward. Gao Wen Zhu quickly followed, not forgetting to explain to the ladies behind her with a smile: "Perhaps it's the cats in heat. These little creatures are just not as refined as humans."

Madame Li Zhuangjin strode to the ear room. Without waiting for the nanny, she kicked the door open with one forceful motion.

"Cui! Yan!"

Madame Li Zhuangjin trembled with rage as she recognized Cui Yan, who had hastily wrapped his middle robe around himself.

She had not even considered the possibility that the man inside might be her son, Gao Yuan. She never expected it to be Cui Yan!

Everyone followed her gaze through the open door. Inside, the brocade quilt on the couch was in disarray, and clothes were scattered all over the floor.

A man in a dark brocade robe was fastening his collar, his shoulders and back glistening with a thin layer of sweat. His sharp, handsome profile was unmistakable; it was Cui Yan.

Beneath him, a woman had her hair in disarray, her hairpins and earrings fallen off. Her water-green ruqun dress was torn askew, revealing her white neck and shoulders.

That coquettish face was none other than Gao Yao, the second miss of the Yongchang Marquis's household.

---

chapters.title: Princess Leshu
chapters.content:
"Crash!" Madame Li Zhuangjin was so enraged that her entire body trembled. She picked up a nearby teacup and smashed it to the ground, the porcelain shards scattering everywhere.

"Presumptuous!"

The loud crash startled the two people on the couch, snapping them completely back to reality.

Cui Yan's face paled as he saw Madame Li Zhuangjin and the crowd of ladies standing at the door. The lust in his eyes vanished instantly.

Gao Yao Jia was so frightened that her soul seemed to leave her body. She let out a shriek and tried to hide in Cui Yan's arms.

The ladies were all stunned. They wanted to pretend they had seen nothing and leave, but it was too late.

"Cui Yan!" Madame Li Zhuangjin's voice trembled with rage as she pointed at him, her hand shaking uncontrollably. "You... how dare you!"

Her eldest daughter, Zhaoyu, was betrothed to Cui Yan. Today, Old Madame Cui had come to discuss the wedding date.

Yet Cui Yan had done such a shameful thing in her marquis's mansion with her second daughter!

Gao Wen Zhu stood behind her mother, watching the scene before her. Her clear eyes showed no ripple of emotion, only a cold chill.

She had long noticed the strange looks exchanged between Cui Yan and her second sister, but she never expected that on such an important day, they would commit such an unforgivable act.

The surrounding ladies understood the situation all too well. They all fell silent, wishing they could shrink into themselves.

"Mother," Gao Wen Zhu stepped forward and tugged at Madame Li Zhuangjin's sleeve, "Old Madame Cui will be here soon."

Madame Li Zhuangjin slapped Gao Wen Zhu's hand away, her eyes cold as she scanned the surrounding ladies. "Good," she said icily. "Go, call the people from the second household to the inner hall."

Madame Li Zhuangjin's servants immediately complied.

Cui Yan looked annoyed. He pushed Gao Yao Jia away from him, his voice hoarse: "Madame, please calm your anger. It was a moment of confusion..."

"Confusion?" Madame Li Zhuangjin let out a cold laugh, the chill in her eyes almost freezing everyone in place. "Are my Gao family's daughters here for you to trample on? Today is Wen Zhu's coming-of-age ceremony, and you come to my rear garden's ear room to do such filthy things with my unmarried daughter's sister! Cui Yan, do you think the Gao family has no one to defend it?"

Gao Yao Jia, pushed to the ground by Cui Yan, collapsed in a heap, crying bitterly. She repeatedly pleaded, "Aunt, spare me... It was Yan Lang who forced me... I didn't mean to..."

Cui Yan suddenly turned to her, his eyes fierce as a blade: "How dare you lie! Clearly, it was you who took the initiative to seduce me time and time again..."

"Enough!" Madame Li Zhuangjin coldly interrupted.

She slowly stepped forward, her gaze sweeping over the two disheveled people on the ground. "Cui Er Lang," she said, emphasizing each word, "today is my Yongchang Marquis's household's Third Miss's coming-of-age ceremony. What you have done. Do you want both the Cui and Gao families to become the laughingstock of the capital?"

---

"What?!" Gao Yuan suddenly stood up, startling the servant boy who had delivered the news. The boy took two steps back in fear.

"Preposterous!" Gao Yuan slammed his fist on the table, sending dishes and soup flying everywhere. "That bastard Cui Yan! My sister treated him with sincerity, and he dares to humiliate her like this!"

Gao Yuan's furious shout startled everyone. The young masters sitting at the same table as Gao Yuan groaned in misfortune and quickly stood up, moving aside.

Gao Yuan was tall, broad-shouldered, and muscular, with a powerful voice from years of martial training. His words echoed through the front hall.

He strode out quickly, and the servant boy, hardening his resolve, intercepted him: "Young Master, please calm down! This matter has already shocked everyone inside and out. If you rush over now, it might..."

"Might what?" Gao Yuan's eyes were bloodshot, his hands clenched into fists, cracking loudly. "That's my own sister! Cui Yan, that beast, did such a shameful thing on my little sister's coming-of-age day, betraying my sister's feelings. If I don't break his legs with my own hands, I'm not worthy of being her brother!"

"Young Master!" The servant boy was so anxious that his forehead was sweating. At this moment, he deeply regretted telling Gao Yuan.

He lowered his voice and urgently advised: "Second Miss is also there! This matter involves the reputation of both families. With the Marquis not in the residence, if you act impulsively..."

Gao Yuan stopped in his tracks, his chest burning with rage.

He closed his eyes tightly and gritted his teeth: "So we just let this go?"

"Not at all. The most urgent thing now is to stabilize the situation and wait for the Marquis to return before making a decision. As for the Cui family... Madame will handle it."

---

The atmosphere in the inner hall had dropped to freezing point.

Madame Li Zhuangjin sat stiffly in the main seat, her face ashen. Gao Wen Zhu stood quietly beside her mother, her gaze fixed on the ground, twisting her handkerchief.

Gao Yao Jia was kneeling in the hall, supported by two rough servant women, her clothes in disarray, sobbing uncontrollably.

Cui Yan stood on the other side, his collar still somewhat disheveled, his face dark enough to drip water.

In the hall, besides the people from the Yongchang Marquis's household, there were also a few noble ladies who had not left; Madame Liu, Madame of Annan County, and several female relatives from the imperial clan who were on good terms with the Yongchang Marquis's household. At this moment, they all kept their eyes downcast, not daring to breathe loudly.

"Mother! Mother, save me!" Gao Yao Jia suddenly cried out toward the door.

Second Madame Zhao hurried in and, upon seeing her daughter in such a disheveled state, her vision went black, and she nearly fainted.

"My child!" Madame Zhao rushed forward to embrace Gao Yao Jia. She turned her head and glared at Madame Li Zhuangjin. "Elder Sister-in-law! What is the meaning of this? What has my Jia done for you to humiliate her like this?"

"Humiliate?" Madame Li Zhuangjin let out a cold laugh. "Second Sister-in-law, why don't you first ask your precious daughter what she has done?"

Madame Zhao was taken aback. Only then did she notice Cui Yan standing in the hall, as well as the evasive glances of the other ladies. Her heart sank.

"Jia..." Madame Zhao's voice trembled as she cupped her daughter's face. "You... you and Cui Er Lang..."

Gao Yao Jia was crying too hard to speak, only shaking her head repeatedly.

Cui Yan suddenly spoke, his voice hoarse: "Today's matter is my fault. I will take responsibility."

"Take responsibility?" Madame Li Zhuangjin turned sharply to face him. "With what? You have a marriage contract with my daughter Zhaoyu. Do you intend to marry the woman beneath you instead?"

Madame Zhao's face turned deathly pale.

Gao Yao Jia also stopped crying, a glimmer of hope appearing in her eyes as she gazed at Cui Yan affectionately.

Cui Yan tightened his lips. After a long pause, he said, "My marriage to Zhaoyu will be explained to my family elders. Since today has already... I naturally should marry Yao Jia."

"You don't even think about it!" A furious shout came from the doorway.

Everyone turned to see Gao Zhaoyu supporting Old Madame Cui, standing at the entrance of the hall.

Gao Zhaoyu's face was as pale as paper, her head lowered, barely maintaining her composure.

Old Madame Cui, leaning on her cane, scanned the crowd in the hall before her gaze settled on Cui Yan. She said in a deep voice, "Ungrateful wretch! Kneel at once!"

Cui Yan stood frozen for a moment before finally kneeling.

Old Madame Cui took step by step into the hall, the sound of her cane striking the floor echoing clearly in the silence.

She sat down in the chair beside Madame Li Zhuangjin and said slowly, "Madame, today's matter is due to my Cui family's failure in teaching. We have brought shame upon the Marquis's household."

Madame Li Zhuangjin took a deep breath. She had no choice but to give Old Madame Cui this face. She forced down her anger: "Old Madame, your words are too heavy. But this matter concerns the reputations of my two daughters. I must ask Old Madame for an explanation."

"An explanation will naturally be given." Old Madame Cui looked at Cui Yan, her eyes sharp. "I ask you, when did you develop a private relationship with Second Miss Gao?"

Cui Yan hung his head. "This grandson... this grandson does not know."

"Do not know?" Old Madame Cui gave a cold laugh. "Then it was Second Miss Gao who took the initiative to seduce you?"

Gao Yao Jia's entire body trembled. She shrilled, "No! I did not! Yan Lang and I are in love with each other!"

"You're lying!" Cui Yan suddenly lifted his head, his eyes filled with bloodshot veins. "Clearly, it was you who sent me sachets and love letters time and time again. Today, it was you who lured me here..."

"So that's how it is..." Gao Zhaoyu suddenly spoke.

She took step by step toward Cui Yan, looking down at him, her voice so soft it was almost inaudible: "So all those rumors were true. During those two years you were at the border, you exchanged letters with her constantly. Every time you came to the mansion, your eyes would always wander toward her. I knew it all... I just didn't want to believe it."

Cui Yan opened his mouth, but no words came out.

Gao Zhaoyu closed her eyes, tears welling in the corners.

She turned and bowed to Madame Li Zhuangjin and Old Madame Cui: "Mother, Old Madame. The marriage between Zhaoyu and Cui Er Lang ends here."

"Zhaoyu!" Old Madame Cui cried out urgently.

Madame Li Zhuangjin cut off Old Madame Cui: "Old Madame, it seems the Gao and Cui families are not fated to be together. The marriage between our families ends here."

chapters.title: Entering as a Concubine
chapters.content:
She spoke with finality, and everyone in the hall was stunned.

Madame Cui sighed heavily. She turned to Li Zhuangjin and said, "Princess, this marriage was personally arranged by Princess Chang years ago. Now that it has come to this, it is the Cui family who has wronged the Gao family and wronged Zhaoyu."

Madame Cui seemed to be backing down, but it made Li Zhuangjin frown.

Li was the imperial surname, and she, Li Zhuangjin, was the daughter of the Prince of Wei, enfeoffed as a princess. The Princess Chang mentioned by Madame Cui was her cousin; Princess Leshuo, the current emperor's sister by blood.

Princess Leshuo was five years older than her and had married into the Cui family, giving birth to Cui Heng, the eldest son of the Cui family. She had intended to arrange a marriage between her daughter and Cui Heng, but Li Zhuangjin's first child was also a son.

So Princess Leshuo had given her word that the second son of the Cui family would marry the first daughter of the Gao family.

Li Zhuangjin was naturally willing.

But she did not expect that Princess Leshuo would pass away in the imperial villa five years later. The year after her death, the head of the Cui family married the daughter of one of the four great families, the Lin family, and gave birth to the second son of the Cui family.

Li Zhuangjin gave birth to a daughter three years after Cui Yan was born. Because of Princess Leshuo's words, seven years ago, the two families officially arranged this marriage.

Li Zhuangjin gently stroked the cloud pattern on her sleeve, listening quietly, and wanted to see what Madame Cui intended to do.

Madame Cui saw that Li Zhuangjin was not responding, paused, and continued, "But things have come to this. Yan'er and the second Miss Gao have already been intimate. If we do not take responsibility, the second Miss Gao's life will be ruined. I shamelessly beg you, can Yan'er marry the second Miss Gao as his wife? As for Zhaoyu..."

Madame Cui looked at Gao Zhaoyu with a kind expression and said, "The Cui family owes you an explanation. I promise here that I will find a better marriage for you. The dowry will be doubled by the Cui family. Are you willing?"

Before Gao Zhaoyu could speak, Zhao shi impatiently interrupted, "Willing! We are willing! Madame, you are so righteous. It is Ka'er's fortune to enter the Cui family!"

"Second Aunt!" Gao Wenchu looked at Zhao shi in disbelief.

Zhao shi ignored her and pushed Gao Yaoke, saying, "Hurry up and thank Madame!"

Gao Yaoke came to her senses and quickly kowtowed, "Thank you, Madame! Thank you, Madame!"

Li Zhuangjin was so angry that her whole body trembled, unable to say a word.

She had not expected the Cui family to be so shameless, ruining her Zhaoyu's marriage, but unwilling to let go of the Gao family's marriage alliance, and even wanting to marry Gao Yaoke!

But then Gao Wenchu spoke softly, "Mother, it is up to Sister to decide her own marriage."

Only then did everyone notice that the other protagonist of this marriage had been quietly standing aside from the beginning, as if she were an outsider.

Gao Wenchu walked to Gao Zhaoyu's side, held her icy hand, and looked up at Madame Cui, "Madame, my eldest sister's marriage is not a bargaining chip. If the Cui family wants to compensate, there are other ways. There is no need to sacrifice my eldest sister's lifelong happiness to atone for Second Sister's mistake."

Her voice was clear, and every word was precious, "Moreover, today's incident happened at my coming-of-age ceremony, ruining the reputation of all the daughters of the Yongchang Marquis's residence. If we settle this matter hastily, others will think that the daughters of the Gao family can be bullied at will."

Madame Cui's gaze flickered.

Gao Wenchu did not evade her gaze and met it directly, "In my opinion, this matter should be discussed together with Father after he returns home. As for Second Sister and Second Young Master Cui..."

She turned to look at the man and woman kneeling on the ground, and a faint smile appeared at the corner of her lips, "Since they are in love and have already consummated their marriage, why not follow Madame's suggestion and fulfill their wishes. However…"

She changed the subject, "The marriage can be arranged, but it must be low-key and simple. After all, it is not a glorious matter. Making a big fuss would only invite ridicule. Since Second Sister is willing, she can marry into the Cui family as a concubine, so that others won't say that the legitimate daughters of the Gao family do not understand the rules and have improper relations with their future brother-in-law."

"Gao Wenchu!" Before Gao Yaoke could react, Zhao shi scolded first, "How dare you let Ka'er marry as a concubine! What are you thinking!"

"Second Aunt," Gao Wenchu turned her head and smiled sweetly, "I am doing this for Second Sister's own good. So many madames have seen it today. If we still hold a grand wedding according to the standards of a legitimate daughter, wouldn't it be telling the entire capital that the daughters of the Gao family can have improper relations with their future brother-in-law at their younger sister's coming-of-age ceremony? Then, how will the other daughters of the Gao family marry in the future?"

Zhao shi was choked into silence and could only glare at her.

Madame Cui pondered for a moment, and her expression towards Gao Wenchu changed. This not only humiliated Gao Yaoke but also humiliated the Cui family.

"Grandmother!" Cui Yan urged.

"Shut up!" Madame Cui scolded harshly, "You have done such a shameful thing. What face do you have to bargain!"

She stood up and said to Li Zhuangjin, "Princess, today we have disturbed Miss Gao's coming-of-age ceremony. I will come to apologize another day. This unfilial son, I will take him back first."

"As for the marriage, the two families still need to discuss it. But we must not harm the harmony between the two families."

Li Zhuangjin nodded numbly. At this moment, her mind was in chaos, and she had no energy to socialize.

Madame Cui left with Cui Yan, leaving only their own people and a few madames who had not left. Madame Liu hesitated again and again before stepping forward and softly said, "Princess, today's matter... we will definitely not spread it."

The other madames also expressed their agreement.

Li Zhuangjin managed to squeeze out a smile, "Thank you all. Wenchu, see the madames out for your mother."

Gao Wenchu obediently agreed and saw the madames out of the inner hall.

Walking in the cloister, Madame Annan could not help but sigh, "Miss Gao, today you have truly impressed me. In such a situation, you were able to keep your composure and say those words."

Gao Wenchu smiled slightly, "Madame flatters me. I just do not want my sister to be wronged."

After seeing off the madames, Gao Wenchu stood in the corridor, looking at the magnolia trees in full bloom in the courtyard, and her expression gradually turned cold.

Today's incident seemed to be an uncontrollable passion between Cui Yan and Gao Yaoke, but the timing was too coincidental.

The coming-of-age ceremony, with all the madames gathered, and Madame Cui about to arrive; coincidentally, at this time, the two of them were having a private meeting in the side room of the back garden and were "coincidentally" caught.

Gao Wenchu recalled that a month ago, she had accidentally seen Gao Yaoke's maid secretly handing a packet of powder to a servant boy next to Cui Yan. At that time, she had thought it was just a common exchange between a man and a woman and did not pay much attention.

Now that she thought about it, that powder... was probably not simple.

"Miss Gao," her close maid Chun Xiao quietly approached and lowered her voice, "The sachet that Second Miss wore today contained 'Warm Love Incense' from the Western Regions."

Gao Wenchu's eyes sharpened.

Indeed.

She lightly exhaled.

This explained everything.

The second branch could not wait any longer.

Gao Yaoke had her coming-of-age ceremony last year, and although her marriage was arranged to the son of the Minister of Personnel, how could that compare to a young master from a prominent family? Seeing that Gao Zhaoyu was about to marry into the Cui family, they took a risky move and used such a despicable method to force Cui Yan to comply.

But they did not expect Gao Zhaoyu to be so resolute and break off the engagement on the spot.

And they certainly did not expect that she, who usually appeared innocent and naive, would take the opportunity to turn the tables and force Gao Yaoke to marry as a concubine.

Presumably, at this moment, Zhao shi and Gao Yaoke were wailing in their room.

A cold smile appeared at the corner of Gao Wenchu's lips.

Did they think they could step on her and her eldest sister to climb up? They had to see if they had the ability.

"Miss Gao, Princess requests your presence." Another maid came to deliver a message.

Gao Wenchu adjusted her sleeves, returning to her usual obedient appearance, and walked towards the inner hall.

In the hall, Li Zhuangjin was holding Gao Zhaoyu and weeping. When she saw her enter, she beckoned her to come over.

Gao Wenchu leaned on her mother's shoulder and softly said, "Mother, don't be sad. Eldest Sister deserves better."

Gao Zhaoyu lowered her head, lost in thought.

Seeing her mother weeping, Gao Zhaoyu sighed and comforted her, "Mother, there is no need to be sad. It is better to see the truth early than to discover it after marriage."

Li Zhuangjin took the handkerchief handed by Gao Zhaoyu and wiped her tears, saying hatefully, "That beast Cui Yan! How dare he treat you like this? If I let the Cui family have their way, I am not Li Zhuangjin!"

Gao Wenchu listened and secretly shook her head. The Gao and Cui families had always been close. If they could not marry Eldest Sister, there was still the second branch. In the end, the outcome of the marriage alliance between the two families would not change.

"Mother, don't be angry. Getting angry at someone like Cui Yan is not worth it." Gao Zhaoyu smiled faintly and poured a cup of tea for Li Zhuangjin, presenting it to her with both hands.

"The Cui family is powerful, but no matter how powerful they are, they cannot and dare not surpass the imperial power. Princess Chang has passed away, and the Cui family is not only ungrateful but also married another daughter from the prominent Lin family. Now they have humiliated my daughter."

Gao Zhaoyu smiled slightly, her gentle and dignified face showing no emotion, "The Cui family... has forgotten whose world this is."

Li Zhuangjin's heart stirred.

Gao Zhaoyu gently held her mother's hand, "Mother, I understand that you feel sorry for me. But since things have come to this, dwelling on it is useless. I only wish for this matter to be resolved as soon as possible and not cause any more trouble."

"How can there be no trouble?" Li Zhuangjin sighed and gave a cold laugh, "The Cui family wants to marry into my Gao family's status, but they also cannot let go of the support from the prominent families. They want both, they are dreaming!"

Before she could finish her sentence, hurried footsteps were heard outside the door. A servant boy ran in, panting, "Madame! The Marquis has returned home! He... he is heading to the second branch's courtyard!"

Li Zhuangjin slowly stood up and glanced at her two daughters, "Let's go."

---

chapters.title: That is the Future of the Cui Family
chapters.content:
In the courtyard of the second branch, the lights were bright.

Yongchang Marquis Gao Jun stood in the hall with his hands behind his back, his face dark and terrifying. Zhao shi knelt on the ground, crying until she was almost out of breath. Gao Yaoke shrunk in the corner, trembling.

"Very good, very good indeed." Gao Jun's voice was not loud, but it carried a bone-chilling coldness, "My Gao family's face has been completely lost by you mother and daughter today!"

"Eldest Brother, please be fair!" Zhao shi crawled forward on her knees, "Ka'er was framed! It was Cui Yan who forced her! How would we, a mother and daughter, dare to offend the Cui family..."

"Framed?" Gao Jun slammed his hand on the table, startling Zhao shi into a tremble, "Was the 'Warm Love Incense' also forced on your daughter by Cui Yan? Was the cleaning servant also planted by Cui Yan?"

Zhao shi's face turned ashen, and she could not speak.

Gao Jun looked down at her, saying each word clearly, "Your husband passed away early, and I have been considerate of your difficulties as a widow and orphan these years, never treating you harshly. Your food, clothing, and daily expenses have all been the same as the first branch. But you? Insatiably greedy, you dare to use such despicable means to climb up to the Cui family, and you chose to do it at Wenchu's coming-of-age ceremony!"

The more he spoke, the angrier he became. He raised his hand and swept the tea set on the table to the floor, "Do you know how the capital will gossip about my Yongchang Marquis's residence after today? How will they gossip about my Gao family's daughters?!"

The sound of shattering porcelain made Gao Yaoke scream.

"Father, please calm down." A gentle voice came from the doorway.

Gao Zhaoyu entered, supporting Li Zhuangjin, followed by Gao Wenchu.

Gao Jun saw his wife and daughters arrive and took a deep breath, forcing down his anger, "Why have you come?"

Li Zhuangjin walked to his side and softly said, "My lord, things have come to this. Anger is useless. The most urgent matter is how to handle the aftermath."

"Handle the aftermath?" Gao Jun gave a cold laugh, "How can we handle it? Are we supposed to let this shameless thing marry into the Cui family and continue to disgrace my Gao family?"

Zhao shi heard this and cried out again, "My lord! If Ka'er does not marry into the Cui family, her life will be ruined!"

"Ruined? She brought it upon herself!" Gao Jun said sternly.

Gao Zhaoyu glanced at Gao Yaoke, who was crying like a pear tree in the rain, and said softly, "Father, Second Sister does deserve punishment. But if we truly do not let her marry, word will spread, and others will only say that my Gao family is harsh to widows and orphans, driving our niece to a dead end. At that time, the damaged reputation will still be that of the Gao family."

Gao Jun frowned and looked at his eldest daughter, "Then what do you suggest?"

"We still have to let her marry." Gao Zhaoyu's voice was gentle and pleasant, like a spring breeze in March, "But we cannot let the Cui family have their way and marry her with great fanfare. Earlier in the inner hall, Wenchu suggested that Second Sister marry as a concubine. Now it seems, that is not enough."

She walked up to Gao Yaoke and looked down at her cousin, "Since Second Sister has chosen to degrade herself, then she shall enter the Cui family as a concubine. A small sedan chair will carry her in through the side gate, the dowry will be halved, and in the future, in the Cui family, she must not consider herself a daughter of the Gao family."

"Gao Zhaoyu!" Gao Yaoke suddenly looked up, her eyes filled with resentment and disbelief, "How dare you humiliate me like this!"

"Humiliate?" Gao Zhaoyu gave a slight smile, "Second Sister, I am saving you. You and your future brother-in-law had improper relations at your younger sister's coming-of-age ceremony. According to the law, you should be drowned. Father and Mother, out of familial love, have spared your life, which is already the ultimate kindness. What, are you still not satisfied?"

Zhao shi wanted to argue, but Li Zhuangjin coldly interrupted, "Second Sister-in-law, Zhaoyu is right. If you are unwilling, tomorrow I will invite the family law and deal with you according to the clan rules."

Zhao shi's body trembled, and she finally collapsed to the ground, weeping incoherently.

Gao Jun pondered for a moment and slowly nodded, "Then we will do as Yu says. The marriage will be simple, and she will enter as a concubine. The dowry... will be reduced by thirty percent."

He looked at Li Zhuangjin, "Madame, tomorrow you will go to the Cui family yourself and make things clear. My Gao family's daughters are not people they can bully at will. If the Cui family does not agree, then this marriage alliance is off. I would like to see if Chancellor Cui dares to take on the reputation of driving a lonely girl to her death!"

"Rest assured, my lord, I understand."

The Cui Family.

Chancellor Cui Yan sat in his study, looking at the marriage contract sent by the Yongchang Marquis's residence, his brows tightly knit.

Madame Cui sat below him and sighed, "Yan'er, we are in the wrong in this matter. The conditions proposed by the Gao family... although harsh, are not unacceptable."

"Mother!" Cui Yan put down the marriage contract, "Entering as a concubine, dowry reduced by thirty percent... this is simply a humiliation! When has my Cui family ever suffered such insults!"

"Then what do you suggest?" Madame Cui said indifferently, "Not marry her? If Gao Yaoke were to take her own life because of this, how would the capital gossip about the Cui family? Forcing an orphaned girl into an improper relationship, leading to her suicide. Can you bear such a reputation?"

Cui Yan was silenced.

Madame Cui continued, "Moreover, Princess Gao, who came today, specially mentioned Princess Leshuo. She said that if Princess Leshuo knew in heaven how the Cui family treated the marriage she personally arranged, she would not know what to think."

Cui Yan's expression changed slightly.

Although Princess Leshuo had passed away many years ago, she was the current emperor's sister by blood and had been greatly favored by the emperor during her lifetime. The current emperor had a deep affection for this sister. When Princess Leshuo passed away, the emperor canceled court for three days, grieving endlessly.

If the Gao family really brought this matter to the emperor's attention...

"Gao family is threatening us." Cui Yan gritted his teeth.

"It is a reminder." Madame Cui corrected, "Reminding us where the Cui family's honor comes from and how it should be maintained."

She stood up and walked to the window, looking at the pines and cypresses in the courtyard, "Yan'er, you married into the Lin family to consolidate the Cui family's position among the prominent families. That is correct. But you must remember that the true foundation of the Cui family is the imperial favor."

"Marrying into the Gao family is not only to fulfill Princess Leshuo's promise but also to show the current emperor that the Cui family has never forgotten its roots."

Madame Cui turned around, her gaze sharp, "Now, although the marriage is with Gao Yaoke instead, the purpose of the marriage alliance has been achieved. As for the manner of the marriage... it is just a matter of face. As long as a Gao family daughter enters the Cui family's door, this marriage alliance is established."

Cui Yan was silent for a long time before finally sighing, "Mother is right. Then... we will do as the Gao family wishes."

The Cui family was a century-old prominent family, and their descendants had always been outstanding, producing two chancellors in just thirty years.

However, the Cui residence was not built luxuriously but exuded a noble and refined elegance everywhere. The corridors were filled with calligraphy and paintings by famous artists, and the courtyard was planted with orchids, bamboo, and other plants symbolizing noble character.

Madame Lin Xueyan, the current mistress of the Cui family, heard about her good son's deeds and was so angry that she gnashed her teeth. She immediately ordered the stewardess to drag Cui Yan over.

The order was given at noon, but by evening, when the marriage contract from the Yongchang Marquis's residence had been delivered, Cui Yan was still nowhere to be found.

Madame Lin's plan to take Cui Yan to the Gao family to apologize and salvage the marriage was completely ruined. Chancellor Cui even ran to the courtyard to scold her for not raising her son properly, which made her so angry that she shouted she would invite the family law to break Cui Yan's legs.

"Mother, Second Brother has really gone too far this time."

Cui Yulan leisurely picked up an orange and started eating, "How can Gao Yaoke compare to Gao Zhaoyu? At the very least, he should have aimed for Gao Wenchu. Now it's too late. Second Brother has been so unmotivated. What can we use to..."

Before she could finish, Madame Lin sharply interrupted, "Enough! Your second brother did not do this on purpose! Instead of criticizing, you should go find him!"

Cui Yulan choked on her orange and sulkily closed her mouth.

"Cui Fu! Have you found Second Young Master yet?!"

The Cui family's steward shrunk as he approached, "Madame, this old servant has ordered the servant boys to search all the places Second Young Master frequently visits, but there is still no sign of him!"

Madame Lin was now anxious. No matter how bad her son was, he was still her son, and she could not let anything happen to him.

"If you can't find him, send more people to look! Useless things, can't even find a person. What use is the Cui family keeping you!"

Madame Lin scolded harshly.

The steward agreed on the surface and quickly took the opportunity to retreat.

Cui Yulan could not help but mutter, "Mother, why are you blaming the servants? Second Brother is so headstrong, who can find him? In my opinion, he must have gone to the brothel to seek pleasure. He will definitely be back tomorrow."

Madame Lin was about to scold her daughter when the maidservant beside her quickly entered and reported, "It's not good, Madame. The young master has been beaten up by someone!"

chapters.title: Cui Yan is Beaten
chapters.content:
Lin Xueyan’s legs gave way, and Cui Yulan, seeing the fallen oranges, quickly supported Lin Xueyan. The two hurried toward the front hall.

Cui Yan had been carried back, now unconscious.

As soon as Lin Xueyan entered the front hall, she saw her son covered in blood. She let out a soft cry, nearly fainting.

"My son…"

"Quick, quick! Send for a doctor!" She rushed to her son’s side, tears streaming down her face. "Yan’er, my Yan’er!"

Cui Yulan was so shocked that she covered her mouth with a handkerchief. Standing a little farther away, she no longer felt any schadenfreude.

"Grandmother, Father." Lin Xueyan’s mind was only on her beaten son, Cui Yan, and she paid no mind to the presence of Old Madam Cui and Cui Yan. Cui Yulan, however, was much calmer. She properly greeted them with a curtsy, and as she rose, her eyes were already filled with tears.

"Grandmother, Father. What happened to Second Brother?"

Cui Yulan wiped away the nonexistent tears and asked weakly.

Cui Yan’s face was ashen as he stared at his unconscious second son on the stretcher, the veins on his forehead throbbing.

He forcibly suppressed his anger and turned to the trembling servant kneeling on the ground: "Speak! What happened?"

The servant was Cui Yan’s personal attendant, Cui An. He was shaking like a leaf, his words stuttering: "R-replying to the master... the young master went to 'Yunxiang Tower'... By the time he came out, it was already dusk. Just as he reached the alley entrance, suddenly, several people rushed out from the shadows. They... they put a sack over the young master’s head and dragged him into the alley..."

"And then?" Cui Yan asked in a deep, measured voice.

"Then they just beat him with fists and kicks... Those people were extremely vicious, aiming for vital spots. I tried to protect the young master, but I was also knocked unconscious..."

Cui An had a grief-stricken look on his face. "When I woke up, the young master was already like this, and those people had long since disappeared without a trace..."

"Did you see who they were?!" Lin Xueyan stood up and asked sharply.

"It was dark, and they had their faces covered... However, one of them had a particularly tall and burly figure, with immense strength. It seemed... it seemed like someone trained in martial arts..."

"Someone trained in martial arts..." Cui Yan repeated softly, a cold glint flashing in his eyes.

Old Madam Cui had been silently sitting at the head of the room, her fingers rapidly moving over her prayer beads.

After a long while, she slowly lifted her head: "Who else could it be?"

The hall fell silent.

Lin Xueyan was stunned, her eyes filled with resentment: "It’s Gao Yuan! It must be that Gao Yuan! He holds a grudge against Yan’er and has resorted to such vicious means! Mother, Master, you must seek justice for Yan’er!"

"Silence!"

Old Madam Cui’s low shout instantly silenced the hall.

She stood up, leaning on her cane, and walked to Cui Yan’s side. She looked down at him for a moment before saying to the hastily arriving imperial physician: "Treat his injuries first."

The imperial physician quickly complied, directing the servants to carefully carry Cui Yan into the inner room.

Only then did Old Madam Cui turn to Cui Yan and Lin Xueyan: "This matter must not be made public."

"Mother!" Lin Xueyan could not believe her ears. "Yan’er has been beaten like this, and we’re just supposed to let it go?!"

"What else can we do if we don’t let it go?"

Old Madam Cui’s gaze was sharp. "Report to the authorities? Let the entire capital know that Cui family’s second young master had an affair with his fiancée’s younger sister, and then, out of guilt, went to a brothel to drink himself into a stupor, only to be ambushed with a sack over his head and have his ribs broken?"

Lin Xueyan was silenced, her face flushed.

"Mother, but this grievance..."

"This grievance must be swallowed, even if it’s hard to bear." Old Madam Cui cut her off. "Today, the Yongchang Marquis’s mansion hastily delivered a marriage contract, and we agreed. If we pursue the matter of Yan’er being beaten now, the Gao family, in protecting Gao Yuan, could completely renege on their promise and make an even bigger scandal out of this. By then, Yan’er would truly be ruined."

She paused, her voice carrying a hint of weariness: "Yan, Xueyan, I know you both are heartbroken for your son. But think about it. Does Yan’er’s actions today do justice to that Zhao girl? Does it do justice to the Cui family’s century-long reputation? Even if the Gao family’s methods were extreme, they had their reasons. If this matter blows up, we will be the ones in the wrong."

Cui Yan’s tightly clenched fists slowly relaxed, his dark expression easing slightly.

The Cui family could not afford this scandal.

Lin Xueyan, however, was still unwilling to accept it, tears welling up in her eyes: "But Yan’er’s injuries..."

"Injuries will heal with time." Old Madam Cui said indifferently. "Let him suffer a little, learn a lesson. It might not be a bad thing."

She looked at Cui Yan: "Tomorrow, you will send someone to the Yongchang Marquis’s mansion."

Cui Yan was taken aback: "Mother means..."

"Take some tonics and say that Yan’er injured himself by accident, and it has nothing to do with the Gao family."

A glint of shrewdness flashed in Old Madam Cui’s eyes. "The marriage will proceed as planned, and everything will be done according to the Gao family’s terms. Be sincere in your attitude and make sure the Gao family feels our sincerity."

Cui Yan instantly understood his mother’s intention, to retreat in order to advance, stabilize the Gao family, save face, and plan for the future.

"This son understands." He bowed in agreement.

Lin Xueyan wanted to say more, but was stopped by a glance from Old Madam Cui.

"Yulan, come with me." Old Madam Cui turned and walked toward the back hall.

Although Lin Xueyan was filled with resentment, she did not dare to disobey and could only signal Cui Yulan to follow.

Old Madam Cui’s residence was very secluded. Previously, whenever Cui Yulan had wanted to come and pay her respects, Old Madam Cui had refused, citing her preference for quiet.

Cui Yulan was now filled with curiosity as she followed her grandmother into the courtyard, which was rarely allowed for the younger generation to enter.

The courtyard was even more serene than the outside, with a faint scent of sandalwood lingering in the air.

Cui Yulan’s heart was uneasy as she wondered why her grandmother had called her alone.

This grandmother of hers came from a scholarly family and had always been the steady matriarch of the household. Even her mother, who came from one of the four great families, the Lin family, often seemed at a loss for words in her presence.

Cui Yulan helped Old Madam Cui sit down on a rosewood armchair, then sat herself at the lower seat, placing her hands neatly on her lap and lowering her eyelids to show a respectful and attentive demeanor.

Old Madam Cui did not speak immediately. She simply looked at Cui Yulan silently for a long time.

Cui Yulan, feeling uncomfortable under her gaze, tentatively said, "Grandmother?"

"Yulan," Old Madam Cui smiled affectionately, "what do you think of today’s events?"

Cui Yulan’s mind raced as she carefully considered her response: "In reply to Grandmother, your granddaughter thinks... Second Brother’s actions were indeed inappropriate, and the Gao family’s anger is understandable. However... Young Master Gao’s actions were a bit too harsh."

"Is that all?" Old Madam Cui took the medicinal tea handed to her by her trusted maid and sipped it lightly.

Cui Yulan hesitated for a moment before probing, "Grandmother, with your discernment, your granddaughter has limited insight. But hearing Mother’s account, I feel... the Gao family’s third young lady, what she said and did today in the inner hall, does not seem like that of an ordinary girl from a boudoir. Second Brother... perhaps truly should not have acted that way."

Old Madam Cui set down her tea cup and smiled: "You can see that Gao Wenju is not ordinary. That makes you more perceptive than your mother."

Cui Yulan’s heart jolted, and she assumed a humble posture, seeking guidance.

"Your mother comes from the Lin family and has high aspirations, but these years of smooth sailing, coupled with the indulgence from your father and Second Brother, have made her lack the wisdom to assess situations properly."

"She only sees that your Second Brother was beaten, but she fails to consider what this incident entails; not just the Yongchang Marquis’s mansion, but more importantly, the Princess and the Wei Prince’s mansion behind her."

Cui Yulan looked up, confusion in her eyes.

"Princess Leshu passed away only a year ago, and the Cui family has already remarried into the Lin family. Now, your Second Brother has done such a disgraceful thing, publicly humiliating the Gao family."

Old Madam Cui slowly continued, "What do you think the Wei Prince and the one in the palace would think?"

Cui Yulan’s face paled slightly: "Grandmother means..."

"The Cui family has had it too easy these years."

Old Madam Cui interrupted her, her gaze intense. "Your grandfather and your father, two generations of prime ministers, have disciples and old subordinates all over the court. The interconnected marriages with prominent families have deep roots. In the eyes of others, it’s a bed of roses; but in the eyes of the one on the dragon throne, it may not be so pleasing."

She looked at Cui Yulan: "The legacy of Princess Leshu is a protective charm for the Cui family, but it could also be a fatal flaw. Used well, it’s a favor; used poorly, it’s a handle for overstepping. The Gao family’s willingness to step back today is not out of fear of the Cui family, but for the sake of the bigger picture."

Cui Yulan listened, her palms growing cold, and her resentment toward Cui Yan deepened. Not only had he competed with her for their mother’s affection, but he had also brought such disaster upon them. He was truly a menace!

"Grandmother... what should we do?" she asked uneasily.

"What to do?" Old Madam Cui gently rubbed the sandalwood prayer beads on her wrist. "We must restrain our ambition and be cautious in speech and action. Gao Yao Jia must enter our family smoothly; this marriage cannot be broken off. As for the future..."

She paused for a moment, then smiled kindly: "Yulan, you are also seventeen this year. It’s time to discuss your marriage."

Cui Yulan was taken aback, not expecting the topic to suddenly shift to herself.

"Your mother has high standards and wants to find you a top-tier family. But a top-tier family may not necessarily be a good thing."

Old Madam Cui looked at her with infinite tenderness. "Sometimes, taking a step back can open up a world of possibilities."

"Grandmother means..."

"What do you think of that Gao Yuan from the Gao family?" Old Madam Cui suddenly asked.

Cui Yulan’s eyes widened almost in disbelief.

"Gao Yuan? He... he beat Second Brother! And he’s ten years older than me!"

"Gao Yuan is the heir to the Yongchang Marquis and will inherit the title in the future. He is upright and values loyalty. Today, he could avenge his sister; tomorrow, he could protect his wife and children."

Old Madam Cui’s words were earnest. "The Gao family may seem to have lost face due to this scandal, but don’t forget, Yongchang Marquis Jian is in the emperor’s favor, and the Wei Prince’s mansion still enjoys imperial grace. The Gao family’s foundation is much more stable than many people think."

She looked at her granddaughter’s shocked expression and slowly said, "Of course, this is just an idea. Your mother may not be willing. But you must remember, the Cui family’s ship is already large enough. Sailing in the eye of the storm, we need ballast. Forming another marriage alliance with the Gao family and truly mending the rift between the two families, that is the long-term plan."

Cui Yulan’s mind was in turmoil. She had never considered marrying someone like Gao Yuan, a blunt and martial man, let alone the fact that he was the "enemy" who had just beaten her second brother.

"This matter is not urgent. Go back and think carefully." Old Madam Cui waved her hand, showing signs of fatigue. "Remember, the words I’ve said to you today must not be told to anyone, including your mother."

"Yes, Granddaughter understands." Cui Yulan hesitated before rising to her feet, bowing, and taking her leave.

As she reached the door, she suddenly remembered something: "Oh, Grandmother, when will Big Brother... return?"

Old Madam Cui’s eyes flickered slightly, and she smiled meaningfully: "Soon."

Cui Yulan nodded in a daze and walked out of her grandmother’s courtyard. A gust of night wind blew, and only then did she realize that her back was covered in a thin layer of sweat.

She turned to look at the silent courtyard, her heart heavy.

Old Madam Cui’s trusted maid took away the medicinal soup. "Old Madam, do not worry. Once the eldest young master returns, everything will be fine."

Old Madam Cui let out a heartfelt laugh: "That... is the future of our Cui family."

chapters.title: Leaving the Capital
chapters.content:
In the study of the Yongchang Marquis's mansion, candles burned brightly.

Gao Yuan knelt stiffly on the ground, the corner of his mouth still bearing the bruise left by Cui Yan's retaliation.

Gao Jun stood in front of him, his face dark with fury, trembling all over.

"Ungrateful wretch! Who told you to go?!" Gao Jun slammed his palm on the table. "Do you have any idea that with this fight, the Gao and Cui families have completely torn apart?!"

Gao Yuan lifted his head, indignant: "Father! But Cui Yan humiliated my sister so. Are we just going to let it slide? You know how my sister has treated him all these years! Yet he dared to do that with Gao Yao Jia at her coming-of-age ceremony! If I didn’t teach him a lesson today, I’d be unworthy of being her brother!"

"Teach him a lesson?" Gao Jun sneered. "Was that teaching him a lesson? Beating him while he was in a sack! Even if Cui Yan was wrong, he is still the legitimate son of the Cui family! You hit him so hard. Do you think the Cui family will let this go?!"

"Let him sue if he wants!" Gao Yuan stuck out his neck. "At worst, I’ll turn myself in to the authorities. An eye for an eye!"

"Nonsense!" Gao Jun raised his hand to strike, but Li Zhuangjin quickly stopped him.

"Lord Marquis, please calm down. Yuan’er was just acting on impulse."

"Impulse?" Gao Jun’s anger did not subside. "His impulse is going to drag the entire marquisate down! This matter was already settled; the Cui family was in the wrong and had to agree to our terms. But now, with Yuan’er’s actions, we are the ones in the wrong!"

"Father," Gao Zhaoyu said softly, "Brother did this for me. If anyone is to blame, it should be me."

Gao Yuan, infuriated by Gao Jun’s attitude, gritted his teeth: "Zhaoyu! This has nothing to do with you!"

Gao Zhaoyu shook her head and knelt beside Gao Yuan. "Father, Brother may be at fault, but Cui Yan insulted a daughter of the Gao family first. Brother stood up for me; it’s only natural. If we must assign blame, I am willing to share it with him."

Gao Jun looked at his children kneeling on the ground, his heart filled with both anger and distress.

"Fools!"

Gao Jun flicked his sleeve and sat down.

Li Zhuangjin observed Gao Jun’s expression and subtly signaled Gao Zhaoyu to rise.

"Lord Marquis, Yuan’er was wrong. Why don’t we go to the Cui family first to apologize? Otherwise, tomorrow they might come here and twist the story, making things worse."

Gao Jun hesitated, waving his hand in refusal. "No. How would that look? The Cui family was at fault first. Why should we apologize?!"

Li Zhuangjin’s lips curled into a cold smile, but her tone softened. "Lord Marquis, your thoughts are exactly mine. They were wrong first, so they likely won’t dare make a big fuss out of this. However..."

She shifted her tone: "Yuan’er was still in the wrong. Why not send him to his maternal grandfather’s place to lie low for a while? Once this matter blows over and both families have calmed down, we can bring him back. It’ll also teach him a lesson."

Gao Jun’s stern face softened slightly, a glint of calculation flashing in his eyes.

"The Prince of Wei is busy with official duties. How can we trouble him with Yuan’er?"

Though he spoke thus, his tone had already mellowed, and he looked up to discuss with Li Zhuangjin.

Li Zhuangjin smiled and gestured for a servant to pour tea.

"How could that be? No matter how busy my brother is, he must take care of his nephew’s affairs. Yuan’er is already twenty-seven and still unmarried; perhaps I should trouble my brother to help find him a match."

Gao Jun’s anger at Gao Yuan’s recklessness had already faded.

Though Gao Yuan was the son of a marquis and a princess, his temper was rash, and his scholarly pursuits were mediocre. He had been idling away his days with a minor sinecure.

Among the noble families in the capital with daughters of similar age, those the Gao family looked up to did not look favorably upon Gao Yuan, and those who looked favorably upon Gao Yuan were not looked up to by the Gao family. Thus, his marriage had been delayed again and again, and to this day, it remained unsettled.

He placed his hand over his wife’s and sighed. "That would be for the best. Even for the sake of the Prince of Wei’s reputation, the Cui family won’t dare make a big fuss. The marquisate’s reputation will be preserved."

Li Zhuangjin and Gao Jun had already decided Gao Yuan’s destination between their exchange. Gao Zhaoyu, hearing this, was relieved and rose with a smile to take her leave.

Gao Yuan, however, panicked. He stood up abruptly and tried to grab Gao Zhaoyu’s sleeve.

"No!" Gao Yuan’s face turned red with anxiety.

Gao Zhaoyu tugged at her sleeve, trying to free herself, and turned back with a gentle smile. "Brother? You’re holding my sleeve."

Gao Jun, seeing this, scowled again. "What are you doing?! Let go of your sister’s sleeve at once. How improper!"

Gao Yuan saw that Li Zhuangjin was about to scold him too and grew desperate. "No, no, I won’t go to the Prince of Wei’s mansion! That place is unbearable! My maternal grandfather and uncles have never liked me, if I go, I won’t have a single good day there..."

"Insolence!" Gao Jun roared. "How many people wish they could enter the Prince of Wei’s mansion, yet you’re the one being picky! Once you’re there, learn properly from your uncles and cousins. You’re almost thirty and still haven’t secured an official position! Are you trying to ruin the Gao family?!"

Gao Jun was furious. What a wasted opportunity! His foolish son didn’t even know how to seize it.

Gao Yuan knew Li Zhuangjin wouldn’t help him, so he pinned all his hopes on his sister Zhaoyu, making faces at her to plead for her intervention.

Gao Zhaoyu looked at her brother, then at her parents, her face filled with difficulty. She struggled to speak: "This..."

"Enough." This time, Li Zhuangjin cut in sternly. "Do you still have the nerve to ask Zhaoyu to speak for you? This matter is not up for discussion. Pack your things; you leave at dawn tomorrow. Once you’re in Xuzhou, study hard. If you waste your time on cockfighting and dog racing instead of proper business, someone will deal with you."

Gao Jun spoke earnestly, hoping to persuade Gao Yuan: "Your mother is right, Yuan’er. You are the only male descendant of the Gao family in this generation, and yet you’ve accomplished nothing. When your father and I are gone, how will we face our ancestors?!"

He looked at his daughter, then back at his son, and sighed in exasperation. "Look at your sister, then look at yourself. Tch!"

Gao Zhaoyu naturally would not stop this. Apart from the fact that her parents’ words made sense, once Cui Yan recovered from his injuries, Gao Yuan staying in the capital would inevitably lead to more conflict. It was better to leave immediately and deny Cui Yan any chance of retaliation.

However... thinking of the Prince of Wei’s family, and then seeing Gao Yuan’s tearful yet helpless expression, and remembering that Gao Yuan had caused this trouble for her sake, Gao Zhaoyu sighed softly.

"Father, Mother, let Wen Zhu go with Brother. It would be good for them to have each other’s company on the road. Wen Zhu hasn’t seen our maternal grandfather and grandmother in a long time; just the other day, she was saying how much she misses them."

Gao Zhaoyu smiled sweetly, finding a companion for Gao Yuan.

Gao Jun’s face lit up as he turned to Li Zhuangjin. "Madam..."

Li Zhuangjin slightly furrowed her brows. She had been planning to find a match for Wen Zhu in the capital...

She looked up at her eldest daughter’s pleading expression and relented. Fine, she would have to prioritize finding a match for Zhaoyu first. Her youngest daughter’s marriage could wait a little longer.

"Very well." Li Zhuangjin nodded. "Tomorrow, Yuan’er and Wen Zhu will leave together. Once in Xuzhou, they are to study hard."

Zhaoyu smiled brightly. "Thank you, Mother. Now Brother can rest assured. Though Wen Zhu is young, she is clever. With her there, Brother will surely not dare to misbehave again, and she can help look out for him in the Prince of Wei’s mansion."

Hearing that Wen Zhu could go with him, Gao Yuan, though still reluctant to go to the Prince of Wei’s mansion, felt slightly better than being sent alone to face punishment. His expression softened a little, and he muttered:

"Then... fine. Where is Wen Zhu? I need to tell her."

"I’ll go tell Wen Zhu." Gao Zhaoyu said gently. "Brother, you should go back and prepare. We leave at dawn tomorrow."

Gao Yuan had no choice but to leave dejectedly, shooting a resentful glance at Zhaoyu. In his mind, he was already scheming how to coax his little sister into covering for his "hobbies" that were far from proper.

Gao Zhaoyu took the opportunity to leave as well, comforting her brother with a few words and lecturing him with some grand principles before heading to her younger sister Wen Zhu’s courtyard.

Left alone in the study were Gao Jun and Li Zhuangjin.

"Madam, letting Wen Zhu go... is it truly alright?" Gao Jun finally showed some unease. He had agreed too quickly just now. "She has just come of age, and her marriage..."

"Marriage is not urgent." Li Zhuangjin’s tone was indifferent. "After today’s events, I see even more clearly that for our daughters’ marriages, we cannot only consider the status of the family. Character, integrity, and family values matter more. The Cui family may appear noble, but they are rotten to the core. Wen Zhu’s marriage must be chosen with even greater care."

She paused, looking at Gao Jun. "Moreover, it would be good for her to stay at the Prince of Wei’s mansion for a while. If she can receive some guidance from your father and my brother, it will only benefit her in the future. Also..."

A cold glint flashed in Li Zhuangjin’s eyes: "Yuan’er’s temper, if no one keeps an eye on him, once he’s in Xuzhou, he’ll likely cause trouble again. Wen Zhu is more steady than Yuan’er. With her there to advise and restrain him, I can rest easier."

Gao Jun nodded, taking his wife’s hand. "As always, Madam, you think of everything. It’s just a shame for Zhaoyu; her marriage..."

At the mention of his eldest daughter, Li Zhuangjin’s expression darkened for a moment before she steeled herself. "Zhaoyu is a child with her own mind. Today, she was able to decisively break off the engagement to preserve her own and the Gao family’s dignity. That kind of character surpasses many men. Her marriage must be chosen with even greater care; we must find someone truly worthy of her."

"You’re right." Gao Jun sighed. "But after this incident, there will surely be much gossip in the capital. It’s unfair to Zhaoyu."

"Gossip?" Li Zhuangjin scoffed. "My daughter is not someone for others to slander. Tomorrow, I will request an audience with Her Majesty the Empress. Zhaoyu’s coming-of-age ceremony was blessed with gifts from the Empress herself."

Gao Jun’s heart stirred. "Madam, you mean..."

"Nothing." Li Zhuangjin subtly withdrew her hand. "It’s just been a while since I paid my respects to Her Majesty. I should visit. Incidentally, let certain people know that the daughters of the Gao family are not to be trifled with."

"Thank you, Madam." Gao Jun said sincerely.

"For our children, it’s no hardship." Li Zhuangjin fell silent. "I only hope that after this, Yuan’er and Wen Zhu will grow, Zhaoyu will find a good match, and all will be safe and happy."

chapters.title: The Graceful Beauty
chapters.content:
"Sister, aren’t you going back? Last month, when Mother read the letter from the Prince of Wei’s mansion, I was by her side. Uncle misses you very much." Gao Wen Zhu was a little excited at the thought of going to Xuzhou.

The Prince of Wei was the current emperor’s uncle, a true hero of his generation, commanding a vast territory. If not for the old emperor’s strong hand, which had temporarily kept the Prince of Wei in check for the current emperor, it might have been someone else sitting on that throne.

Gao Wen Zhu chatted idly with her sister, asking Gao Zhaoyu about the Prince of Wei’s mansion.

Gao Zhaoyu had spent a long time at the Prince of Wei’s mansion when she was young, only returning to the capital four years ago. No one in the capital knew more about the Prince of Wei’s mansion than she did.

Gao Wen Zhu had been eagerly waiting for her sister to tell her about the Prince of Wei’s mansion, but after a long wait, Gao Zhaoyu only managed to say a few words:

"The Prince of Wei’s mansion... is magnificent. Our maternal grandfather is a very imposing man. He has four sons, two daughters, and many nephews and nieces..."

A flicker of doubt passed through Gao Wen Zhu’s eyes.

She laughed cheerfully and continued the conversation: "Sister, you stayed at the Prince of Wei’s mansion for six years. Why aren’t you going back with us this time?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, she answered herself: "Oh, Sister, look at me; I forgot again."

Gao Zhaoyu was nineteen this year, a little past the usual marriageable age. It was just that Li Zhuangjin was reluctant to let her daughter marry so soon. She had only been by her side for a few years when she discovered the affair between Cui Yan and Gao Yao Jia...

Gao Zhaoyu smiled, unconcerned. "It’s nothing. But I truly cannot go with you and Brother. Mother still needs to find a husband for me. Xuzhou is near the border, and though the climate is dry, the scenery is nice. When you get there, remember to moisturize and drink plenty of water, or your skin will dry out."

Gao Wen Zhu tilted her head, feeling that something was off with her sister. Maybe she was affected by the marriage issue, Gao Wen Zhu thought.

But her sister had always been known for her talent, and though her appearance was not stunning, she was still a graceful beauty. How could she lack suitors?

She giggled. "I know. I used to regret not having the chance to see Uncle, but I never expected that Brother’s outburst would actually fulfill my wish."

Gao Wen Zhu did not miss the maternal grandfather she had never met, but she was very curious about the uncle who had inherited the title of Prince of Wei.

The Prince of Wei had been a romantic figure in his lifetime, with many children. Yet, the title of Worldly Prince had been bestowed upon his youngest son.

Since she had started reading, she had known about this uncle, known as a once-in-a-generation genius. She had also heard that he had inherited the Prince of Wei’s looks.

A close friend had once told her, with a dreamy expression, that she had caught a glimpse of him from afar three years ago; a man of vigorous bearing...

Wen Zhu loved heroes, especially those who were both literary and martial, handsome, and dashing...

"Uncle is indeed an extraordinary man." Gao Zhaoyu’s soft voice pulled Gao Wen Zhu back from her thoughts. "Wen Zhu, our maternal grandfather is old and has a fiery temper. You must be careful with your words and actions in the mansion. Though the Prince of Wei and the other uncles are good people, they are reserved and not fond of talking. Don’t think they are cold to you if they don’t speak much."

Gao Wen Zhu blinked. "Sister, the way you say it only makes me more curious. The other uncles are all married, but I’ve heard that the Prince of Wei is twenty-nine and still unmarried. Countless noble ladies, both in the capital and Xuzhou, secretly admire him, yet he doesn’t even glance their way. Do you know why?"

Gao Zhaoyu’s fingers unconsciously twisted the handkerchief in her hands. She smiled. "The Prince of Wei is deep in thought. He has his own considerations. Don’t ask too much about these things, and don’t discuss them in front of others."

"Alright." Gao Wen Zhu laughed and agreed, then looped her arm around Zhaoyu’s, pulling her into more talk about the Prince of Wei’s mansion.

After a while more of conversation, Gao Zhaoyu took her leave, urging Wen Zhu to prepare her luggage and rest early.

As soon as Gao Zhaoyu returned to her courtyard, she saw Li Mama, her mother’s trusted maid, waiting for her.

"Mama, why didn’t you come in? The night is deep and the dew is heavy; be careful not to catch a cold."

Gao Zhaoyu’s lips curved into a faint smile as she invited Li Mama inside.

"Thank you for your concern, Miss. I only came to deliver a message. I’ll leave as soon as I’m done; I won’t disturb your rest." Li Mama smiled warmly and gave a slight bow.

"Did Mother have any instructions?" Zhaoyu asked with a smile.

"In reply to Miss, the Princess Consort wishes to enter the palace tomorrow to pay her respects to Her Majesty the Empress. She sent me to ask if you would like to accompany her."

Gao Zhaoyu’s smile faltered. After a few seconds of thought, she shook her head. "No. Please tell Mother that I have an appointment with Scholar Chen tomorrow to discuss music. I’m afraid I won’t be able to accompany her."

She sighed helplessly. "Besides, I just broke off my engagement today. If I enter the palace tomorrow, it might invite unnecessary gossip."

Li Mama respectfully acknowledged the order. "Yes, I will relay your words truthfully to the Princess Consort. Then, Miss, please rest early. I will take my leave."

After watching Li Mama leave, Gao Zhaoyu’s smile gradually faded. She turned and went back inside.

Qing Dai stepped forward to remove her hairpins and jewelry, then asked softly, "Miss, are you really going to Scholar Chen’s tomorrow?"

Gao Zhaoyu looked at her reflection in the mirror, her plain face appearing especially cold in the candlelight.

"No. Go to the Chen family and send word that I’m unwell. I’ll visit another day to seek his guidance."

"Yes." Qing Dai agreed, then hesitated. "Then, Miss, tomorrow..."

"I’ll stay in the courtyard. I won’t go anywhere." Gao Zhaoyu removed her earrings herself. "Tell the gatekeeper to close the doors and refuse all visitors. I won’t see anyone."

Qing Dai did not dare to persuade her further and complied.

After Qing Dai left and closed the door, Gao Zhaoyu sat alone at her dressing table, lost in thought.

She reached out and gently touched the white jade hairpin on the table. As her fingertips brushed the smooth jade, a wave of panic and irritation surged in her heart.

Snap;

The jade hairpin was lightly tossed into the drawer by Gao Zhaoyu. She blew out the remaining candles.

---

The next morning, Gao Yuan and Gao Wen Zhu were quietly sent out of the capital. Gao Zhaoyu went back to sleep and woke up to find that Li Zhuangjin had already entered the palace.

Gao Zhaoyu stayed in her courtyard with the doors closed. It wasn’t until noon that she came out to the veranda to play the guqin. The melody was elegant but carried a hint of melancholy.

When the piece ended, she stopped playing and rose, flicking her sleeve.

"Miss," Qing Dai approached with tea and snacks, speaking softly. "The gatekeeper just reported that the Cui family has sent someone with a card."

Gao Zhaoyu took a sip and asked calmly, "What kind of card?"

"It’s a wedding invitation from the Cui family’s second young master and second young lady." Qing Dai answered indignantly.

Miss had treated those two so well, yet they were ungrateful wretches!

Gao Zhaoyu took the gilded invitation and opened it. It read that on the ninth day of the ninth month, Cui Yan would marry Gao Yao Jia.

There were still half a year to go.

Gao Zhaoyu closed the invitation and said indifferently, "Send it to the second branch."

"Miss, are you alright?" Qing Dai asked worriedly. It would be hard for anyone to bear if their own cousin stole their fiancé, let alone Miss, who had always been proud and dignified.

"I’m fine." Gao Zhaoyu slowly shook her head.

After a moment of thought, she spoke slowly: "Go to the warehouse and take a pair of jade Ruyi scepters. Add them to my second sister’s dowry. Say... it’s my gift to her."

Qing Dai was taken aback and immediately felt indignant on her mistress’s behalf. "Miss, after what Second Miss did to you, you still..."

"One thing has nothing to do with the other." Gao Zhaoyu cut her off. "We were sisters. The proper etiquette must be observed; I cannot neglect it."

Qing Dai’s eyes welled up. "Miss, you’re just too kind. That’s why they could bully you like that..."

Kind?

Gao Zhaoyu shook her head with a light laugh.

She wasn’t kind. Gao Yao Jia was wrong, but she was still a daughter of the Gao family. If she were to kick her while she was down, it would only give outsiders more reason to mock the Gao family.

Moreover, Gao Yao Jia was already being punished by being married as a concubine. Life in the Cui family would not be easy for her in the future.

"Go." She waved her hand.

Qing Dai took the invitation and left.

Gao Zhaoyu sat back down and began to play the guqin again, her fingertips lightly plucking the strings, the music flowing like water.

chapters.title: Man Unmarried, Woman Unwed
chapters.content:
Kunning Palace.

Empress Xiao sat upright in the main seat. Upon seeing Li Zhuangjin enter, she smiled and raised her hand. "Zhuangjin, you've arrived. Please, take a seat."

Li Zhuangjin bowed. "This humble subject's wife greets Her Majesty the Empress."

"Dispense with the formalities." Empress Xiao gestured for the palace attendants to offer a seat. "Must we still stand on ceremony between us? It's been a long time since we last met. How have you been?"

"Thanks to Your Majesty's blessings, all is well."

Li Zhuangjin smiled faintly and got straight to the point. "Today, I take the liberty of requesting an audience. First, it has been too long since I last paid my respects to Your Majesty, and I have been concerned. Second..."

She paused, her face clouded with worry. "Your Majesty must have heard about my daughter, Zhaoyu's marriage..."

Empress Xiao had indeed heard. Her nephew had been invited to the Yongchang Marquis's residence the day before for the capping ceremony of the third Miss Gao. Upon returning, he had complained to his parents about Gao Yuan overturning the table, nearly implicating him.

She nodded slightly. "I have heard some whispers. That boy from the Cui family is truly unreasonable."

"Your Majesty sees clearly." Li Zhuangjin's eyes reddened slightly. "Zhaoyu is a clever and sensible child who has never caused me any worry. She only returned to the capital at fourteen, and I was reluctant to let her marry so soon, so I kept her for a year or two longer. Who could have imagined... such a thing would happen. Now that the marriage is called off, rumors are spreading throughout the capital. I am truly worried."

Empress Xiao sighed softly. "I have met Zhaoyu a few times. She is a good child. The second son of the Cui family doesn't know how to behave. Rest assured, I will take care of this matter for her."

Li Zhuangjin immediately stood up and bowed. "On behalf of my daughter, this humble subject's wife thanks Your Majesty for your grace."

"Sit down and talk." Empress Xiao waved her hand, indicating that she need not be so formal.

"Speaking of coincidences, Jianzhi will be returning to the capital soon.
