That child left the capital at a young age to study, and after becoming the top scholar, he requested to be posted away to Xuzhou. Now he is twenty-seven and still has no one by his side. I think Zhaoyu and Jianzhi would make a perfect match."

Li Zhuangjin had not expected Empress Xiao to find a match for Zhaoyu so quickly. Upon hearing the name, she was stunned for a moment.

After a long while, she finally spoke softly. "Jianzhi? Is he the son of Princess Changshu?"

Empress Xiao smiled and nodded. "Yes, Jianzhi is his courtesy name, given by Mr. Lu Ning from the Hanlin Academy during his capping ceremony. He has been posted away for ten years, and His Majesty has long wanted him to return to the capital."

Li Zhuangjin frowned and forced a smile. "This... might not be appropriate. Princess Changshu's son is also surnamed Cui. He is the elder brother of Cui Yan. Zhaoyu just broke off her engagement with Cui Yan, and now she is to be engaged to his elder brother..."

Empress Xiao waved her hand. "Zhuangjin, you worry too much. His Majesty and I both think Jianzhi and Zhaoyu are a perfect match. They are both unmarried, talented, and good-looking. What could be inappropriate? Moreover, you and Princess Changshu are not only cousins but also close friends. If your children marry, wouldn't that make you even closer?"

Seeing that Li Zhuangjin still wanted to decline, Empress Xiao's voice deepened. "Zhuangjin, nothing is more important than the happiness and safety of our children. Jianzhi is a man of great learning and fine appearance. At such a young age, he has already reached the fourth rank in officialdom. All of this is due to his real talent and hard work. By the way, they are also cousins by marriage. Isn't this a wonderful match?"

Li Zhuangjin's heart trembled.

Jianzhi was Cui Heng, the only son of Princess Leshu, the eldest son of the Cui family.

That child who had been expected to achieve great things since childhood, who passed the imperial examinations at thirteen, became the top scholar at seventeen, and then requested to be posted away to Xuzhou for ten years...

But...

"Your Majesty," Li Zhuangjin struggled to speak, "Jianzhi is indeed an exceptional young man, but..."

"What is it?" Empress Xiao picked up her tea cup, took a sip, and looked up at her. "Zhuangjin, you are a clever woman. You should understand what I mean."

Li Zhuangjin's palms began to sweat. She was not foolish and could certainly hear and see the intentions of the emperor and empress.

Of course, she understood.

Although Cui Heng and Cui Yan were brothers, they were as different as night and day. Cui Yan was born of the Lin family, while Cui Heng was the only son of Princess Leshu, a true noble of imperial blood. After being posted away for ten years, he was now returning and would certainly occupy a place in the court.

By marrying Zhaoyu to him, they could maintain the marriage alliance between the Cui and Gao families and also establish a deeper connection with the imperial family through Cui Heng.

"Your Majesty," she gave a bitter smile, "this humble subject's wife understands Your Majesty's kind intentions. However... this matter still requires careful consideration. Zhaoyu has just experienced the pain of a broken engagement. Discussing marriage now may..."

"I understand." Empress Xiao set down her tea cup and slowly said, "I am telling you this today so that you are aware. Jianzhi's return to the capital will still take some time. You can take your time to think about it. But Zhuangjin..."

She looked at Li Zhuangjin with a meaningful gaze. "Some opportunities, once missed, are difficult to find again."

"This humble subject's wife... understands."

As she left Kunning Palace, Li Zhuangjin's steps were unsteady.

Outside the palace gates, the Gao family's carriage had been waiting for a long time. When Li Mama saw her pale face, she quickly stepped forward to support her. "Princess, are you alright?"

"I'm fine." Li Zhuangjin waved her hand and got into the carriage.

Inside the carriage, she leaned against the cushion and closed her eyes in deep thought.

Cui Heng... Jianzhi...

She recalled the grand scene of Princess Leshu's marriage to the Cui family over twenty years ago. The ten-mile red dowry, the city-wide celebrations; it was the most glorious wedding she had ever seen.

At that time, she and Princess Leshu were both noblewomen of the imperial family and were always together.

"Zhuangjin, if we have children in the future, we must make them in-laws."

Later, when Princess Leshu became pregnant, Li Zhuangjin often visited the Cui residence. During the delivery, she closely watched for any possible mishaps. Finally, Princess Leshu safely gave birth to the child. But who could have predicted that Princess Leshu would pass away just two years later...

At that time, Cui Heng was only two years old and probably didn't even remember his mother's face.

She held that child and wept bitterly.

Later, Cui Yan married Lin, and she gradually drifted apart from the Cui family. She only occasionally encountered Cui Heng, watching him grow from a silent and reserved child into a talented and brilliant young man.

Ten years ago, after he became the top scholar and requested to leave the capital, she never saw him again. Li Zhuangjin now tried to recall, but she could no longer remember what the child looked like.

"Madam, we have arrived." Li Mama's voice came through.

Li Zhuangjin collected her thoughts, adjusted her clothes, and, with Li Mama's support, alighted from the carriage.

In front of the marquis's residence, Gao Zhaoyu had already received the news and was waiting at the gate.

"Mother, you're back."

She came forward and spoke gently.

Li Zhuangjin took her daughter's hand and walked inside, only nodding.

Gao Zhaoyu noticed her mother's unusual expression and asked softly, "What did Her Majesty the Empress say?"

Li Zhuangjin looked at her daughter's beautiful face, her heart filled with countless thoughts, which she could only express with a soft sigh.

"Let's talk inside."

Gao Zhaoyu felt something was amiss but ultimately said nothing, quietly entering the main house with her mother.

"Zhaoyu," Li Zhuangjin sat down for a moment before finally speaking, "If... your mother finds a better marriage for you, would you be willing?"

Gao Zhaoyu's steps faltered slightly, and she turned to look at her mother. "A better marriage?"

"Yes." Li Zhuangjin sighed softly and slowly nodded. "Better than Cui Yan, better than any young master from the noble families in the capital."

Gao Zhaoyu was silent for a moment, then suddenly smiled. "Mother, are you talking about the Prince of Wei's residence?"

Li Zhuangjin was taken aback and then shook her head. "No."

"Not?" Gao Zhaoyu was surprised.

"It's Cui Heng." Although Li Zhuangjin didn't know how her daughter had thought of the Prince of Wei's residence, she still told Zhaoyu about the empress's intentions today. "The son of Princess Leshu, the eldest son of the Cui family, Cui Yan's elder brother."

The smile on Gao Zhaoyu's face froze.

"Cui... Heng?"

Li Zhuangjin hummed in agreement. "Her Majesty the Empress mentioned him today. She said he will return to the capital soon. Her Majesty thinks you and he are a perfect match."

Gao Zhaoyu stood frozen in place, unable to speak for a long time.

Cui Heng.

Of course, she knew of him.

That legendary eldest son of the Cui family, the son of Princess Leshu, who passed the imperial examinations at thirteen, became the top scholar at seventeen, and then requested to be posted away to Xuzhou for ten years. Her teacher had spoken of him with great pride, only because he had once taught Cui Heng a few lessons.

"A talent capable of managing the affairs of the world." Zhaoyu unconsciously murmured the words.

When she was at the Prince of Wei's residence, she had once seen him from afar a few times.

At that time, he was already in his early twenties, dressed in a blue robe, with cold and clear features. He stood alone at the end of the corridor, gazing at the magnolia tree in the courtyard, lost in thought.

The servants of the prince's residence said that he was the eldest young master of the Cui family, who had come to Xuzhou for studies.

Later, she learned that it was not for studies, but for his posting.

"Mother," Gao Zhaoyu came back to her senses and carefully considered her words, "This... doesn't seem appropriate. I just broke off my engagement with Cui Yan, and now I am to marry his elder brother. What will others think?"

"Her Majesty the Empress said that you are both unmarried, talented, and good-looking. There is nothing inappropriate."

Li Zhuangjin took her daughter's hand. "Zhaoyu, I know this is sudden. But you must understand that Cui Heng is different from Cui Yan. He is the son of Princess Leshu, His Majesty's own nephew. If you marry him, you will be the daughter-in-law of Princess Leshu and the future matriarch of the Cui family."

"But..." Gao Zhaoyu hesitated.

"Zhaoyu," Li Zhuangjin looked into her daughter's eyes, "Tell your mother honestly, do you have someone in your heart?"

Gao Zhaoyu's heart trembled, and she instinctively denied it.

"No."

"Truly not?" Li Zhuangjin asked suspiciously. If there was no one, then it would be easy to handle.

Seeing Gao Zhaoyu deny it again, Li Zhuangjin sighed softly. "Do you know why Her Majesty the Empress wants to arrange a marriage between you and Cui Heng?"

Gao Zhaoyu nodded and then shook her head.

"Because Cui Heng is the son of Princess Leshu."

Li Zhuangjin spoke seriously. "He is His Majesty's own nephew. Unlike the people of the Prince of Wei's residence, he poses no threat to His Majesty. Her Majesty the Empress's words are His Majesty's words. His Majesty wants him to marry you not only to maintain the marriage alliance between the Cui and Gao families but also to..."

She paused and sighed softly. "To restrain the Prince of Wei's residence."

Gao Zhaoyu's eyebrows furrowed slightly, and she fiddled with the handkerchief in her hands.

"His Majesty has always been wary of the Prince of Wei's residence." Li Zhuangjin slowly said. "The Prince of Wei is stationed in Xuzhou with heavy troops, and the heir apparent is also an extraordinary figure. His Majesty cannot help but be cautious. However, the Prince of Wei is after all the imperial uncle, so His Majesty cannot act too excessively."

"So His Majesty wants to use a marriage alliance to counterbalance the Prince of Wei's residence?" Li Zhuangjin shook her head. "Not only that. If Cui Heng marries you, it will be an alliance between the Cui and Gao families, as well as a bridge between His Majesty and the Prince of Wei's residence. He can both restrain the Prince of Wei's residence and balance the power of the noble families. It is a move that achieves multiple goals."

Gao Zhaoyu understood.

In this game of chess, she had once again become a pawn.

Gao Zhaoyu lowered her eyelids.

The Gao family appeared prosperous but was in fact walking on thin ice. Although the Yongchang Marquis enjoyed imperial favor, he was still a subject. The Prince of Wei's residence could be the Gao family's glory or their shackles. If His Majesty truly wanted to make things difficult, the Gao family would have no means to fight back.

"I understand, Mother."

Gao Zhaoyu softly parted her lips. "I am willing."

"You..." Li Zhuangjin stopped mid-sentence.

"I am not acting on impulse." Gao Zhaoyu smiled slightly. "I have thought it through. Marrying into the Cui family is beneficial for the Gao family, and for me... it is also not a bad match."

"But Cui Heng..."

"Although I do not know Eldest Young Master Cui well, I have heard of his reputation." Gao Zhaoyu lightly smiled. "If he is unwilling, no one can force him. If he agrees..."

She paused, her voice as gentle as a breeze. "Then I will marry him."

Li Zhuangjin's heart was filled with mixed emotions.

"Zhaoyu, you have suffered." She embraced her daughter, choking back tears.

Gao Zhaoyu gently patted her mother's back, a smile on her lips.

What was there to suffer? After all, she had to marry someone, and Cui Heng had always had a good reputation. There was no need for her to worry about her future husband.

chapters.title: The Incident
chapters.content:
"Young Master... it's best you don't go in..." The servant seemed to have something difficult to say, stammering as he spoke.

Xu Anju still had no idea what had happened. The triennial spring imperial examinations were approaching, and he had been studying day and night, hoping to pass with flying colors and bring honor to his family. But today, as soon as he stepped out, he noticed the servants looking uneasy, whispering among themselves. Uneasy, he hurried to the courtyard outside his parents' quarters, only to be blocked by the servant.

"Why? What has happened in the residence?" Xu Anju asked anxiously, his scholarly demeanor evident.

The servant was caught in a dilemma. The master and mistress had ordered that the young master must not be told of this matter.

"Young Master, please return to your studies. The master has important matters to attend to and has ordered that he is not to be disturbed."

Xu Anju was filled with doubts, but he didn't want to disturb his father's important business, so he left reluctantly, looking back several times as he went.

Inside the main house of the Xu residence, Gao Jun, with a pained and apologetic expression, confessed to Minister Xu of his negligence in guiding his niece, which had led her to commit such a disgraceful act.

Minister Xu and his wife exchanged silent glances but could not blame Gao Jun. They managed only a few perfunctory words.

"Worthy brother, I, Gao Jun, have come today fully prepared."

Gao Jun cupped his hands, his face filled with sorrow. "All the blame lies with my Gao family. Yao Jia... it was my failure to discipline her that led her to commit such a shameful act that dishonors our family name. Today, I stand here to apologize. As for the marriage agreement... I leave it to the Minister's residence to decide."

Minister Xu of the Ministry of Personnel, now in his fifties, had some gray in his hair and beard. After a long silence, he finally spoke slowly, "Lord Yongchang, your words are too heavy. Marriage between children is about mutual affection and heavenly destiny. Since Miss Gao Jia... has someone else in her heart, we Xus are not the kind to force the matter."

Though he spoke thus, the fingers holding his teacup had turned slightly white.

Madame Xu, née Wang, had red-rimmed eyes as she forced back her tears. She had always liked Gao Yao Jia, finding the girl clever and a good match for her own gentle and mild son. Who could have imagined...

"The letter of marriage dissolution will be sent to your residence later," Minister Xu stood up. "From now on, the marriage agreement between our families is void. Each will go their separate ways in marriage."

Gao Jun bowed deeply. "Your noble character is greatly appreciated by me, Gao. If there is anything the Gao family can assist with in the future, do not hesitate to ask."

It was thought that the matter would end there, but paper cannot wrap up fire forever. Xu Anju eventually found out about the farce. After hearing the news, he fell seriously ill. The sudden blow left him bedridden, unable to recover.

Within a short month, the promising young scholar, who had a bright future ahead, died of depression. He never got to take the imperial examinations that year. A marriage that had not yet been formally concluded ended with the death of another.

Enraged by the loss of his beloved son, Minister Xu exposed the dark secrets of the Gao and Cui families to the court, sparking a storm of political intrigue and bloodshed.

---

The Yongchang Marquis' residence had been eerily silent for half a month. The servants held their breath, not daring to make a sound, fearing they might incur the displeasure of Gao Jun and Li Zhuangjin.

Since the Gao family had been reported, the Emperor had flown into a rage. Although he had saved some face for the Gao family on the surface, the Brocade Guard had received a secret order from the Emperor to investigate the Yongchang Marquis' case.

The courtyard of the second branch was particularly silent.

Gao Yao Jia was locked in her room, crying all day. Lady Zhao, though heartbroken for her daughter, did not dare to defy the Marquis and the Eldest Daughter-in-law. She could only sit with her daughter and weep.

"Mother, I don't want to marry as a concubine..." Gao Yao Jia cried, her eyes red and swollen. "I am the second miss of the Yongchang Marquis' residence. How can I be carried into the Cui family in a small sedan chair like those lowly concubines..."

Lady Zhao wiped her tears. "What use is there in saying this now? After what you've done, it's a miracle you're still alive. Your uncle said that if you don't want to marry, you will be dealt with according to the family rules... How can I bear to watch that happen to you..."

"But Cui Yan promised to marry me as his wife!" Gao Yao Jia grabbed her mother's hand. "He said he would take responsibility for me!"

"Responsibility?" Lady Zhao gave a bitter laugh. "He can't even save himself now. You've driven the Xu family's young master to his death, and now the entire Marquis' residence is dragged into this because of you!"

Gao Yao Jia's eyes flashed with resentment. "It's all Gao Zhaoyu's fault! It must be her causing trouble! And Gao Wen Zhu, that little vixen, acts so innocent and sweet every day, but she's so vicious at critical moments!"

Lady Zhao looked at her daughter, who was still deceiving herself even now, and couldn't help but sigh. "Don't say anything else. If the Gao family can't get through this, it's not just about marrying into the Cui family. Even our past days will be gone."

Gao Yao Jia's eyes finally flickered.

That gentle and refined Xu Anju had indeed treated her well. But what she had always wanted was not the son of a Minister of Personnel. She wanted a legitimate heir of a prominent family, a husband who could bring her endless glory.

Cui Yan... should have been hers.

If it weren't for Gao Zhaoyu standing in her way...

"Mother," Gao Yao Jia suddenly lowered her voice. "Is it true that... Cui Yan's elder brother is coming back?"

Lady Zhao was taken aback. "You mean Cui Heng? What about him?"

Gao Yao Jia's eyes flashed with a hint of calculation. "Cui Heng is the son of Princess Leshu. His status is not much lower than Cui Yan's. If... if I could marry him..."

"You've gone mad!" Lady Zhao covered her mouth in shock. "You've just had that affair with Cui Yan, and now you want to set your sights on his elder brother? Moreover, who do you think Cui Heng is? Would he even consider you?"

"Why not?" Gao Yao Jia pushed her mother's hand away, her eyes filled with unwillingness. "I'm younger than Gao Zhaoyu, and more beautiful than her. Why can she marry, and I can't? Besides... Cui Yan is already ruined. The future of the Cui family depends on Cui Heng. If I can climb up to him..."

"Stop it!" Lady Zhao sharply interrupted her. "Aren't you causing enough trouble already? If you have any more wicked ideas, you'll completely provoke your uncle and the Princess Consort. You won't even be able to keep your life!"

Gao Yao Jia bit her lip and fell silent, but her eyes were filled with defiance.

She was not resigned to this.

Why could Gao Zhaoyu gain the Empress's favor? Why could Gao Wen Zhu live a carefree life in the Prince of Wei's residence? They were all daughters of the Gao family. Why should she suffer such humiliation?

In her indignation, a thought suddenly struck her. She excitedly grabbed Lady Zhao's hand.

"Mother, I've got it! I know how to save the Gao family!"

Seeing that Lady Zhao did not believe her, she quickly got up and tried to run out, but was pulled back by Lady Zhao.

"Mother, I'm serious! I really have a way! Go and tell my uncle what I said. If we perform a meritorious deed to redeem our sins, the Yongchang Marquis' residence can escape this predicament, and I can still marry Cui Yan as his wife!"

Gao Yao Jia laughed wildly.

"Why does His Majesty want to investigate the Yongchang Marquis' residence? Is it really because the Marquis abused his power and embezzled funds?" she said with a meaningful and sinister smile. "There are so many corrupt officials. Why does His Majesty investigate only us? The reason His Majesty is investigating our Gao family is because..."

Lady Zhao was confused by her daughter's words, thinking that Gao Yao Jia had gone mad.

"Mother, listen to me. Go and tell my uncle. Have Gao Zhaoyu marry Cui Heng, and I guarantee that our Gao family will be safe!"

Gao Yao Jia stood up unsteadily, laughing crazily. "His Majesty doesn't want to go through the trouble of investigating corruption. So many corrupt officials are left unchecked, yet he specifically targets our Marquis' residence? Mother, think about it. Who stands behind the Yongchang Marquis' residence? It's the Prince of Wei's residence!"

Lady Zhao was startled, and her face turned pale.

Gao Yao Jia lowered her voice and extended her index finger, putting on an air of mystery. "His Majesty has been wary of the Prince of Wei's residence for a long time. The Prince of Wei is stationed in Xuzhou, holding military power, and the heir apparent is exceptionally talented. How can His Majesty sleep peacefully? His investigation of the Yongchang Marquis' residence is just a warning to the Prince of Wei. His true purpose is to reduce the Prince of Wei's power and suppress the heir apparent's influence!"

"So, if our Gao family wants to escape this predicament, we must let His Majesty know that we are on his side!"

"How can we prove it? Who should a daughter of the Gao family marry to make His Majesty feel at ease? Not Cui Yan, nor any heir of a prominent family, but. Cui Heng!"

"Cui Heng is the son of Princess Leshu, His Majesty's own nephew! He represents His Majesty's side! If Gao Zhaoyu marries him, it would be equivalent to the Gao family siding with His Majesty! In that case, what reason would His Majesty have to continue making things difficult for the Gao family? Perhaps he might even reward our 'loyalty'!"

Lady Zhao was stunned by her daughter's words, a chill rising in her heart. Though the words were crazy, they were not entirely without reason. In the imperial court, the situation was complex and ever-changing, and the Emperor's intentions were unfathomable.

The current predicament of the Yongchang Marquis' residence might indeed not stem from those scandals, but from the overly illustrious backing behind it.

"But... but would Cui Heng be willing? What about the Empress..."

"The Empress summoned the Princess Consort to the palace today. Maybe that's her intention!" Gao Yao Jia exclaimed excitedly. "Mother, go quickly and tell my uncle. Tell him exactly what I said! If we can arrange the marriage between Gao Zhaoyu and Cui Heng, the Gao family will surely turn the tide! By then, I will be the 'meritorious official' who made this happen. My uncle and the Princess Consort will have to acknowledge my contribution. My marriage... will naturally be conducted with the rites of a primary wife!"

Lady Zhao looked at the fanatical light in her daughter's eyes, her mind in turmoil. But now, she and Yao Jia were on the brink of an abyss. Maybe... it was worth a try?

She gritted her teeth and made up her mind. "Alright, I'll go and talk to your uncle now. You stay here. Don't go anywhere, and don't say anything!"

Gao Yao Jia watched her mother's retreating figure and a twisted smile appeared on her face.

chapters.title: To Xuzhou
chapters.content:
Gao Yuan and Gao WenZhu arrived in Xuzhou on the second day after the incident in the capital.

The courtyard of the Prince of Wei’s residence was vast and deep. Gao WenZhu was settled in a separate small courtyard called "Qixia Yuan." The courtyard was exquisite, with several Western Fu begonia trees planted inside, now in full bloom, clustering together in a most beautiful display.

The maidservant leading the way, whose surname was Zhou, was a trusted aide of the Prince of Wei’s consort. She smiled warmly and introduced, "Cousin Miss, this Qixia Yuan is not far from Her Highness’s 'Ruifu Hall.' Just pass through that moon gate, and you’ll be there. Her Highness specifically ordered that Young Master and Miss be settled comfortably."

Gao WenZhu thanked her with a smile and ordered Chun Xiao to reward Madam Zhou.

The main house had three rooms, with side rooms on both sides. The furnishings were elegant but not extravagant. A few pieces of porcelain from the previous dynasty were displayed on the multi-treasure pavilion, and the walls were adorned with landscape paintings, the inscriptions of which were by the hand of a renowned contemporary master.

"Miss, the Prince of Wei’s residence is indeed extraordinary," Chun Xiao said softly while organizing the luggage. "Look at this bed canopy; it’s Ruanyan silk from Jiangnan, a tribute item. Even in the capital, it’s hard to find a single bolt."

Gao WenZhu ran her fingers over the canopy, but her thoughts were elsewhere.

"Chun Xiao," she suddenly asked, "where has my brother been settled?"

"Young Master is staying in 'Songtao Yuan,' which is two courtyards away from here, near the outer study," Chun Xiao replied. "Earlier, I heard Madam Zhou say that the Heir Apparent ordered that Young Master start studying with the Prince’s private tutor tomorrow."

Gao WenZhu nodded. Although her brother Gao Yuan was reluctant, now that they were in the Prince of Wei’s residence, he had no choice but to comply.

The evening banquet was set in the Prince’s "Juxian Hall."

Gao WenZhu changed into a goose-yellow embroidered dress with folded magnolia branches, her hair styled in a simple double-ring bun, adorned with a pair of pearl hairpins, exuding a lively and youthful charm.

Prince Wei sat at the head of the table, with his consort seated beside him. To their lower left was the Heir Apparent, Li JinYun, followed by the Prince’s other three sons and their families. Gao Yuan sat below Li JinYun, looking constrained, and made faces at her when he saw her arrive.

Gao WenZhu ignored him and properly greeted everyone with a curtsy. The Prince’s consort pulled her to sit beside her.

"WenZhu, you’ve come of age this year, haven’t you?" the Prince’s consort asked with a smile. Though she was sixty years old, her voice was still strong and clear. "Time flies so quickly. The last time I saw you, your mother brought you back for a visit. You were only three or four years old, a tiny little thing who loved clinging to your cousin JinYun for sweets."

Everyone in the hall laughed.

Gao WenZhu’s cheeks flushed slightly as she glanced at Li JinYun. He was holding a wine cup, and upon hearing this, the corners of his lips lifted slightly, though the smile did not reach his eyes.

"Grandmother has a good memory," she replied obediently. "WenZhu doesn’t remember much from back then."

"You were too young then, so it’s natural you don’t recall," the Prince’s consort said affectionately, patting her hand. "From now on, while you’re staying in the residence, spend more time with your grandmother. How is your mother?"

"Mother is well, though she often misses Grandfather and Grandmother," Gao WenZhu replied. "Before I left, she especially told me to express her filial piety on her behalf."

The Prince’s consort nodded in satisfaction.

Midway through the banquet, Li JinYun suddenly spoke: "In the capital, did WenZhu often spend time with ZhaoYu?"

The hall fell silent for a moment.

Gao WenZhu, however, maintained her smile. "In reply to Cousin Heir Apparent, my elder sister is busy with her studies in music, chess, calligraphy, and painting. Though I often go to her for guidance, I’m too dull to learn even half of what she knows."

"ZhaoYu has been clever since she was a child," the Prince’s consort took over. "It’s been five years since we last saw her. Your grandfather and I miss her dearly!"

Prince Wei remained silent, merely chuckling.

Gao WenZhu smiled gently. "Elder sister misses you and Grandfather too. It’s just that she’s busy with her wedding preparations and couldn’t come."

Li JinYun lowered his gaze, lightly swirling the wine in his cup.

Prince Wei laughed heartily: "His Majesty and Her Majesty the Empress are kind and loving. It is ZhaoYu’s fortune. Come, eat. This perch was caught from Yunze Lake just this morning; it’s very fresh."

The topic shifted, and the banquet continued.

Gao WenZhu secretly let out a breath, but she felt a gaze on her. She looked up and met Li JinYun’s deep, inscrutable eyes.

His expression was complex and unreadable. In an instant, he averted his gaze.

Gao WenZhu felt an inexplicable pressure. She picked up a small piece of fish and put it in her mouth. The meat was indeed fresh and delicious.

The Heir Apparent of Prince Wei was truly impressive in both appearance and demeanor, she thought.

---

At the same time, in the capital’s Yongchang Marquis Residence.

Gao ZhaoYu sat alone in the courtyard, playing the guqin under the moonlight.

Qing Dai approached quietly and draped an outer robe over her shoulders. "Miss, it’s late. Be careful not to catch a cold."

Gao ZhaoYu stopped playing. "What time is it?"

"It’s the third quarter of the Hai hour," Qing Dai replied softly. "Earlier, the gatekeeper reported that the Cui family sent more tonics. They said it’s for the Second Miss’s dowry."

Gao ZhaoYu sneered. "The Cui family is suddenly so attentive."

Ever since the Cui and Gao families were simultaneously impeached, the Cui family had shown unusual enthusiasm for Gao YaoJia’s marriage. Tonics, fabrics, jewelry; they sent batches every few days, making a great show of their goodwill.

Qing Dai lowered her voice: "When the Marquis returned from court today, his expression was terrible. I heard that Minister Xu publicly impeached the Cui family in court for poor family management and allowing their son to commit atrocities. By extension, our Marquis Residence..."

Gao ZhaoYu’s fingers twitched slightly.

Xu AnJu’s death had become a thorn in Minister Xu’s heart. The old minister, having lost his beloved son, no longer cared about official decorum and was determined to seek justice.

Qing Dai was deeply worried. "Miss, will this matter implicate our Marquis Residence?"

"It already has," Gao ZhaoYu stood up, looking toward the imperial palace.

The Emperor’s attitude would determine the fate of the Gao family.

She suddenly recalled what the Empress had said to her mother the other day, that Cui Heng would return to the capital soon.

If Cui Heng returned now, it would add another piece to this game of chess.

"Qing Dai," she suddenly said, "go fetch paper and a brush."

"Miss, are you writing a letter?"

"Write to WenZhu," Gao ZhaoYu walked toward the desk. "She’s just arrived in Xuzhou, and I’m rather worried about her."

She dipped the brush in ink and hovered over the paper, but hesitated for a long time.

Gao ZhaoYu suddenly realized she didn’t know what to write.

Should she report peace? In this situation, what peace was there to speak of?

Should she confide her feelings? How could she express the secrets buried deep in her heart?

In the end, she only wrote a few ordinary greetings, urging WenZhu to take care of her health and listen to their grandfather and grandmother.

After finishing the letter, she sealed it and handed it to Qing Dai.

"Send it to the post station first thing tomorrow morning."

"Yes."

After Qing Dai left, Gao ZhaoYu sat alone by the lamp, staring at the flickering candlelight, lost in thought.

She suddenly remembered the year she turned fourteen, in the rear garden of the Prince of Wei’s residence, when Li JinYun had reached out to remove a fallen flower from her hair, and the warmth of his fingertips.

---

Xuzhou, Prince of Wei’s Residence, Study Room.

Li JinYun sat at his desk, holding a secret letter.

The candlelight cast shadows on his face, outlining his stern features. He read the contents of the letter for a long time, then brought the paper close to the candle flame.

The flame flared up, instantly consuming the paper.

"Your Highness," a trusted guard reported in a low voice from outside the door. "News from the capital: Minister Xu launched another attack in court today. His Majesty has ordered the Three Courts to jointly investigate the Cui and Gao families."

Li JinYun looked up. "How has the Yongchang Marquis Residence responded?"

"The Marquis claimed illness and did not attend court. The Princess entered the palace this afternoon and has not yet returned," the guard replied. "Additionally, according to our informant, Young Master Cui Heng’s carriage has already reached Hejian Prefecture and will arrive in the capital soon."

Cui Heng was returning to the capital.

Li JinYun tapped his fingers lightly on the desk, deep in thought.

Cui Heng had been away from the capital for ten years. In Xuzhou, his political achievements were remarkable, yet he had always maintained a low profile, never drawing attention to himself.

Now, his sudden return to the capital was suspicious in its timing.

"Keep watching."

Recalling the contents of the secret letter, Li JinYun’s knuckles tightened, turning white.

If that person was a good match, so be it. But Cui Yan...

A cold glint flashed in his eyes.

Was such a man worthy of her?

"JinYun."

A voice came from behind him.

Li JinYun composed himself. "Father."

Prince Wei entered the study and gestured for him to sit. "You’ve heard about the capital?"

"Just received the news."

Prince Wei stroked his chin thoughtfully. "Minister Xu is going all out. The Gao family is in trouble this time."

"What does Father think?"

"The Gao family cannot fall," Prince Wei said gravely. "The Yongchang Marquis holds a special place in His Majesty’s heart, and the Princess is a royal relative. The Gao family is the link between the Prince of Wei’s residence and the capital."

Li JinYun remained silent.

The Prince of Wei’s residence, stationed in Xuzhou, commanded a powerful army and had long been viewed with suspicion by the Emperor. If the Gao family fell, the Prince of Wei would lose a crucial support in the court.

"Cui Heng’s return to the capital is a variable," Prince Wei continued. "He is highly capable, and you’ve had dealings with him in Xuzhou. Moreover, he is the son of the Grand Princess, and His Majesty holds him in high regard. If he sides with the Gao family, there might be a turn for the better."

"Father thinks Cui Heng will help the Gao family?"

"Not necessarily," Prince Wei shook his head. "But the Empress has expressed interest in matching him with Gao ZhaoYu."

Li JinYun’s throat tightened.

"Is the marriage decided?"

"Not yet, but the Empress has hinted at it to the Princess," Prince Wei said, looking at his son. "JinYun, I know what you’re thinking. But some things cannot be forced."

Li JinYun lowered his gaze. "This son understands."

"That’s good," Prince Wei patted his shoulder. "The future of the Prince of Wei’s residence rests on you. When it comes to matters of the heart, let go when you must."

Let go when you must.

Easier said than done.

Li JinYun’s heart grew cold.

---

chapters.title: Return to the Capital
chapters.content:
On the official road from Hejian Prefecture to the capital, a procession of carriages and horses traveled at a steady pace.

It was late spring, and the willows along the road swayed gently, the grass lush and green.

At the front was a simple green-curtained carriage, unadorned except for a subtle "Cui" emblem carved on the shaft.

Inside, Cui Heng sat with his eyes closed, resting.

He wore a plain light green straight robe, tied at the waist with a dark sash, and no jade decorations. Ten years of exile had left little trace of hardship on his face, instead adding a calm and composed demeanor.

His eyebrows were like strokes of ink, his eyes like cold stars, his nose high and straight, his lips well-defined. Though his face should have been stern, his bearing lent it a touch of warmth.

"Young Master, we’re approaching the Ten-Li Pavilion," a servant outside reported softly.

Cui Heng slowly opened his eyes and lifted the carriage curtain to look outside.

The Ten-Li Pavilion was a place on the outskirts of the capital for farewells and welcomes. At this moment, several carriages were already parked outside, with a dozen or so people waiting beside them. Leading them was Cui Fu, the steward of the Cui residence, followed by several managers and servants.

As Cui Heng’s carriage approached, Cui Fu quickly led the group forward and bowed. "This old servant welcomes Young Master back to the capital."

Cui Heng stepped out of the carriage and gestured lightly in acknowledgment. "Uncle Fu, no need for such formalities."

"Old Master and Old Madam have been waiting in the residence for a long time," Cui Fu said, looking up at the young master he had not seen in ten years. In his heart, he sighed. After ten years, Young Master had become even more steady and composed. His entire demeanor surpassed even the Old Master in his youth.

Cui Heng nodded slightly, his gaze sweeping over the crowd. "Thank you all for your trouble."

Cui Fu personally took the reins and drove, softly reporting the recent events in the capital.

"The Second Young Master’s matters... Old Master and Old Madam are very worried," Cui Fu said quietly. "The Yongchang Marquis Residence has taken a firm stance. The matter of the Second Miss Gao entering the family as a concubine is already settled."

Cui Heng’s expression did not change; he merely gave a faint "mm."

The carriage entered the capital, passing through the bustling streets, and finally stopped in front of the Cui residence.

The Cui residence was just as he remembered; tall red gates, imposing stone lions. Only the plaque above the gate seemed to have been freshly painted, the gilded characters "Cui Residence" gleaming under the spring sunlight.

Cui Heng stepped out of the carriage and stood at the gate, looking up at the plaque for a long time without speaking.

Ten years.

He had finally returned.

"Young Master, please," Cui Fu bowed and led the way.

Cui Heng collected his thoughts and stepped over the threshold.

The scenery inside the residence was unchanged; winding corridors, lush trees and flowers. The servants, seeing his return, stopped to bow, their eyes filled with curiosity.

When they reached the main hall, Cui Yan and Old Madam Cui were already waiting in the seats of honor. Lin XueYan stood beside Old Madam Cui, while Cui Yan and Cui YuLan accompanied them on the lower seats.

"Grandson greets Grandmother and Father," Cui Heng said, stopping in the middle of the hall, lowering his gaze, and bowing with cupped hands.

Then he turned to Lin XueYan. "Greetings, Mother."

Old Madam Cui looked at him, her eyes filling with tears. "Heng, get up. Let your grandmother have a good look at you."

Cui Heng stood up and walked to Old Madam Cui. She took his hand and looked him up and down, her voice choking. "You’ve gotten thinner and darker. These years in Xuzhou, you’ve suffered."

"Not at all," Cui Heng replied, taking her hand in return, his voice gentle. "The people of Xuzhou are simple and honest. Though the official duties were busy, they were fulfilling."

Cui Yan looked at his eldest son, his heart filled with a mix of emotions.

This son had always been different. After Grand Princess Leshu passed away, he had become even more silent, yet he had never neglected his studies. He passed the imperial examinations at thirteen, became the top scholar at seventeen, and then requested to be sent away, leaving for ten years.

During those ten years, he had achieved remarkable political accomplishments in Xuzhou, yet he never boasted. The court reports about him were full of praise. Now that he had returned, he was already known as a "pillar of the nation" by His Majesty himself.

"It’s good that you’re back," Cui Yan managed a kind smile. "You must be tired from the journey. Sit down and talk."

Cui Heng took a seat at the lower position as instructed. Cui YuLan personally served him tea. "Elder brother, have some tea."

"Thank you, younger sister," Cui Heng took the cup and sipped lightly.

Lin XueYan looked at the father and son, her heart filled with bittersweet emotions. Why was the difference between her two sons so great?

"Heng," Old Madam Cui wiped her tears, her emotions overwhelming. "Now that you’re back, you won’t leave again, will you?"

Cui Heng set down his tea cup and smiled warmly. "This grandson still needs to fulfill his filial duties to you and Father."

"Good, good," Old Madam Cui sighed in relief. "As long as you have that heart, it’s enough!"

Old Madam Cui was more than satisfied. With a filial and capable grandson like this, the future of the Cui family was secure.

Cui Yan’s brow furrowed slightly.

He changed the subject. "You must have heard about the recent matters involving the Cui and Gao families."

Cui Heng nodded, a hint of worry in his eyes. "Will this matter shake the foundations of the Cui family?"

"It shouldn’t," Cui Yan shook his head. "His Majesty’s actions are meant as a warning, not a true punishment. But the Gao family... The Yongchang Marquis Residence has the Prince of Wei behind it. His Majesty’s attitude toward the Prince of Wei..."

Cui Heng’s gaze flickered.

"Heng," Old Madam Cui suddenly asked, "are you familiar with the Prince of Wei’s Heir Apparent?"

"We’ve had some official interactions, met a few times," Cui Heng replied. "The Heir Apparent is exceptionally talented, strict in military discipline, and highly respected in Xuzhou."

Old Madam Cui nodded and said no more.

A brief silence fell over the hall.

Cui YuLan, seeing this, smiled to break the silence. "Elder brother must be exhausted from the journey. Why not return to your courtyard to rest? We can talk more at dinner."

Cui Heng took the opportunity to rise. "Very well. This grandson will take his leave."

"Go on," Old Madam Cui said affectionately. "Your courtyard has always been kept ready, cleaned every day."

Cui Heng bowed and took his leave. As he passed Cui Yan, who wore a gloomy expression, he nodded and smiled in greeting. Cui Yan scoffed and looked away.

Cui Heng’s smile remained unchanged. Under Cui Fu’s guidance, he walked toward his former courtyard.

As he passed through the familiar corridors, he paused slightly when he reached the garden.

The magnolia tree in the garden was in full bloom, its flowers as white as snow.

"Young Master?" Cui Fu noticed him stop and called softly.

Cui Heng withdrew his gaze. "Let’s go."

The courtyard retained its appearance from ten years ago; every plant and tree unchanged. As he pushed open the door, the room was bright and clean, the furnishings as they had been, as if the master had never left.

Cui Heng walked to the desk and ran his fingers over the smooth surface.

This had once been where he studied and practiced calligraphy.

Cui Fu looked at the young master before him, recalling his master’s concerns, and felt a surge of emotion.

"Young Master, you must be tired from the journey. Rest early. This old servant will take his leave," Cui Fu bowed.

Cui Heng nodded gently, signaling Cui Fu to withdraw.

The night wind began to rise, stirring the loose strands of hair at his forehead.

Cui Heng snapped out of his thoughts and stood up to close the window. He clasped his hands behind his back, standing quietly as he gazed at the Cui residence under the night sky. A faint smile appeared on his lips, but his eyes remained as deep and cold as a pool, unmoved even by the night wind.

chapters.title: Choosing Him as a Son-in-Law is Not Impossible
chapters.content:
Gao Zhaoyu walked along the West Market Street with Qing Dai, her steps much slower than usual.

Since breaking off her engagement with Cui Yan, this was the first time she had left the house.

"Miss, 'Mo Yun Zhai' is just ahead," Qing Dai softly reminded her. "The Xie Xin Tang paper and pine soot ink you wanted should arrive today."

Gao Zhaoyu nodded slightly, but her gaze was somewhat distracted. Chen Sixuan, the younger sister of the Minister of Revenue, was a close friend of hers. Yesterday, Chen had sent a letter inviting her to meet at Mingyue Tower today.

Chen Sixuan’s letter was written in haste, the handwriting so messy it almost clung together. Gao Zhaoyu held the letter, her heart heavy, vaguely guessing that it was likely about her marriage troubles again.

Since it was a close friend’s invitation, and she had indeed not been out for a long time, she wrote a reply agreeing to meet at the third quarter of noon today, and also decided to stop by Song Mo Zhai to buy some paper and ink.

Lost in thought, a sudden commotion arose ahead. A few mischievous boys chased each other out of an alley, nearly knocking over an elderly flower seller. The old woman’s bamboo basket tilted, and several half-bloomed magnolia flowers scattered on the ground.

Gao Zhaoyu instinctively stepped back, but something slipped from her sleeve, landing with a light ding on the ground.

It was a white jade hairpin.

The hairpin rolled twice on the ground before stopping at the feet of a man wearing dark brocade boots.

Gao Zhaoyu looked up and met a pair of calm eyes.

The man bent down and picked up the hairpin, unhurried.

The midday sunlight happened to fall on his shoulders, outlining his slightly thin figure.

He was around twenty years old, with an exceptionally handsome face and a smile in his eyes; truly living up to the phrase "as refined as jade." What was most striking was his demeanor, though he appeared young, he carried a settled calmness.

He simply stood there, and Gao Zhaoyu felt as if the entire bustling street had fallen silent.

When he handed the hairpin back, the noise in her heart also suddenly subsided.

"Miss, your hairpin." His voice was clear and smooth, like jade striking stone.

Gao Zhaoyu was momentarily stunned, blankly staring into the man’s slightly teasing eyes before she snapped back to reality and quickly took it.

"Thank you, young master." She nodded with restraint.

The noon sun was fierce, warming her face until it felt slightly scorching.

"You’re welcome." The man replied gently, the smile in his eyes seemingly fading a little.

Gao Zhaoyu gave a slight nod. She should have left, but inexplicably, she asked an extra question: "Is Young Master also here to buy paper and ink?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, Gao Zhaoyu regretted them. This street had more than just Song Mo Zhai, and there were passersby; her question was out of place.

Yet the man answered with surprising familiarity: "Yes."

Gao Zhaoyu’s face flushed even more at the sound of his voice. She lightly coughed to cover her embarrassment and turned her face away. "Then I won’t disturb you further. Qing Dai, let’s go."

"Wait a moment."

Gao Zhaoyu had just turned away when the voice spoke again, warm yet hesitant.

She paused, slightly turning her head but not looking at him.

"Does Young Master have something to ask?"

She already had a guess in her mind. The imperial examinations had just concluded, and many successful young scholars were temporarily staying in the capital, waiting for official appointments and assignments.

Though this man was composed, he carried the air of a scholar who had just achieved success. He had a natural scholarly aura, yet she had never seen him in the portrait albums her mother had shown her for selecting a husband. He must be one of the newly successful scholars.

Gao Zhaoyu thought his appearance was fine, his voice... was also quite pleasant. If she chose him as a husband, it might not be a bad idea...

The man, however, did not speak. He remained standing in place, the afternoon sunlight gilding his dark gray robe with a faint gold.

He slightly raised his hand and pointed at her sleeve: "Miss, your handkerchief seems to have come loose just now."

Gao Zhaoyu looked down and saw that the moon-white handkerchief embroidered with orchids at her waist had indeed slipped from its sash due to her earlier retreat and turn, one corner dangling, about to fall.

She hastily raised her hand to tie it, but her fingers, flustered, were not very nimble. The knot of the sash was intricate, and she struggled to retie it.

At that moment, a long-fingered hand reached out, not touching her or the handkerchief, but merely gesturing in the air: "This knot is untied like this."

His voice was not loud, yet it clearly cut through the faint noise of the street and reached her ears.

"Hook your left index finger here, and gently push this loop with your right thumb."

Gao Zhaoyu followed his instructions, and indeed, the knot loosened slightly. She focused on fixing it, her long lashes casting a faint shadow beneath her eyes, completely unaware that the man’s gaze was quietly resting on her profile.

After much effort, Gao Zhaoyu finally retied the handkerchief. She lifted her head, regaining her usual composure.

"Thank you for your guidance, Young Master." She thanked him with restraint.

The man’s lips slightly curled: "It was nothing."

He paused, his gaze sweeping past the sign of Mo Yun Zhai behind her. "Is Miss here to purchase stationery?"

"That’s right." Gao Zhaoyu’s proudly raised head gave a slight nod.

"The Xie Xin Tang paper at Mo Yun Zhai is indeed of fine quality. However, the recent delay in the southern grain transport has also delayed the new shipment of paper, which may take a few more days. If Miss is in urgent need, you might consider going to 'Wen Hua Ge' on East Street. They received a new batch just the day before yesterday. Though the stock is limited, the paper quality is excellent."

"Young Master seems quite knowledgeable about paper and ink." She couldn’t help but say.

"Just a little." He answered modestly, a smile playing on his lips. "An elder in my family has a fondness for such things. I’ve merely picked it up through exposure."

This aligned with her guess.

With that, he said no more and turned to leave.

"Young Master." Gao Zhaoyu suddenly spoke, not knowing why she had called out to him.

He stopped and turned, slightly narrowing his eyes.

The sunlight was just right. The elderly flower seller had rearranged her basket, and the faint fragrance of magnolias wafted through the air.

Gao Zhaoyu met his calm gaze, and after a moment, she revealed her first smile of the day, parting her lips slightly: "I haven’t yet asked for Young Master’s surname."

The man stood still for a moment before a faint, indescribable curve appeared at the corner of his lips.

"My humble surname is Cui." He said, his eyes brimming with a smile. "My given name is a single character, Heng."

Cui Heng.

The two characters, light and simple, yet like a stone dropped into a still lake, rippled through Gao Zhaoyu’s heart.

By the time she recovered from her shock, Cui Heng had already turned and merged into the crowd, his figure gradually disappearing into the distance.

So it was him.

So this was how they met.

"Cui Heng will return to the capital soon."

Gao Zhaoyu’s subconscious step forward halted.

She turned to look, but the long street was bustling with people, the sunlight just right, yet the figure in dark clothing was already gone.

Qing Dai looked puzzled: "Miss?"

"Nothing." Gao Zhaoyu withdrew her gaze, but a smile unconsciously curved her lips.

She suddenly felt that today’s sunlight was exceptionally clear.

"Cui... Heng."

Gao Zhaoyu slowly uttered the two words.

---

chapters.title: Why Worry About Not Being Independent
chapters.content:
Inside the elegant room of Mingyue Tower, Chen Sixuan had been waiting for a long time.

She leaned against the window, absentmindedly twisting her handkerchief, her gaze occasionally drifting to the bustling street below. Today, she had used the excuse of visiting a temple to offer incense to slip out, bringing only a trusted maidservant with her.

The door creaked open.

"Zhaoyu!" Chen Sixuan’s eyes lit up as she quickly stepped forward. "You’ve finally arrived."

Gao Zhaoyu removed her veil hat, and Qing Dai took it, retreating to stand guard outside the door. She carefully observed Chen Sixuan, noticing the faint dark circles under her eyes and the unmistakable anxiety in her expression.

"Sixuan, you’ve lost weight." Gao Zhaoyu took her hand, which felt slightly cold.

Chen Sixuan forced a smile and pulled her to sit by the window. "Please, sit. I’ve ordered the cloud mist tea you like, along with some pastries."

The aroma of tea wafted through the air. Gao Zhaoyu did not immediately press for answers but quietly poured tea for both of them.

After a moment of silence, Chen Sixuan spoke, her voice slightly hoarse: "My brother... is going to finalize my marriage."

Gao Zhaoyu’s hand paused. "Who is the man?"

"Liu Mingcheng, the Assistant Minister of Works." Chen Sixuan bit her lip, her eyes glistening with tears. "He’s thirty-five years old, widowed, with one son and two daughters. His late wife... died in childbirth with their youngest daughter."

Gao Zhaoyu’s brows furrowed tightly.

She knew Chen Sixuan’s brother was a smooth operator, always playing both sides in the official circles, single-mindedly focused on advancing his career, and had never paid much attention to his younger sister.

The Assistant Minister of Works was a fifth-rank official, but at that age, he was eighteen years older than Chen Sixuan, and this was a second marriage...

"My brother says that though Director Liu is older, his future is promising, and his household has no concubines; he’s a dependable man."

Chen Sixuan’s voice grew softer and softer. "But I... I’ve barely even seen him. I only remember catching a glimpse of him from afar at Xu Jiejie’s wedding banquet last year. He’s short and plump, and when he talks, spittle flies everywhere..."

Suddenly, she grabbed Gao Zhaoyu’s hand, her fingertips icy. "Zhaoyu, I don’t want to marry him. I’m only seventeen. Why should I have to marry a man so much older and become a stepmother to his three children?"

Gao Zhaoyu gripped her hand in return. "Why is your brother in such a hurry?"

Chen Sixuan gave a bitter laugh. "Liu Mingcheng is a disciple of the Right Chancellor. My brother in the Ministry of Revenue has been heavily suppressed by the Left Chancellor’s faction lately. If he can establish a connection with the Right Chancellor..."

Gao Zhaoyu sighed inwardly.

The head of the Cui family, Cui Yan, was indeed the Right Chancellor, holding a position second only to the Emperor, with disciples and subordinates throughout the court; far beyond what the Left Chancellor could match.

But ever since more than half a month ago, when the Cui and Gao families were publicly accused by Director Xu in court, demanding the Emperor’s intervention, though the Cui family remained powerful and stable, unlike the Gao family’s turmoil, their influence had still been suppressed, primarily by the Left Chancellor’s faction.

"I’ve quarreled with my brother for several days. He locked me in the courtyard and wouldn’t let me out."

Chen Sixuan wiped her eyes. "My mother passed away early, and my father doesn’t interfere. In this household... my brother makes all the decisions. Today, I only managed to slip out by pretending to go to the temple to hold a memorial for my mother."

She looked up at Gao Zhaoyu with tearful eyes. "Zhaoyu, what should I do? Your marriage... well, even if it fell through with the Cui family, your parents dote on you. There will always be other options. But me? I’m supposed to marry a man nearly forty with a house full of children!"

Gao Zhaoyu felt a pang of sorrow.

She knew Chen Sixuan had it hard; her father and brother didn’t care, and her sister-in-law was always scheming to marry her off. Yet she was gentle and indecisive, especially when it came to matters of marriage, unable to take control of her own fate.

"Sixuan," Gao Zhaoyu said softly, "do you have... someone you admire?"

Chen Sixuan was taken aback for a moment before her expression darkened again. "What does it matter if I do or don’t? My brother wouldn’t care."

"If you do have someone you admire, perhaps we can find a way for him to propose. As long as his family background is decent, your brother might not insist on the Liu family’s proposal."

Chen Sixuan shook her head, tears rolling down her cheeks as she sobbed, "It’s useless. He... he’s a student at the Imperial Academy, from a poor family, and he failed the imperial examinations this spring. My brother would never agree."

Gao Zhaoyu fell silent.

The gap between social classes was like an unbridgeable chasm.

"Zhaoyu, I truly envy you." Chen Sixuan suddenly said. "Even though Cui Yan is no good, your family background is excellent, and you’re clever and beautiful. Unlike me..."

Gao Zhaoyu cut her off with a bitter smile. "Sixuan, you mustn’t belittle yourself. While it’s true that marriages are arranged by parents and matchmakers, your mother is gone, your father is in the countryside, and your brother hasn’t fulfilled his duty as an elder brother. Instead, he wants to use your marriage to climb the social ladder and curry favor with the powerful. Since he’s neither kind nor just, why must you obediently follow his orders?"

Chen Sixuan froze.

She had come to meet Gao Zhaoyu today with a glimmer of hope, but she had never considered defying her brother...

"But, but what can I do? I’m just a woman. I don’t know anything. Without my brother and sister-in-law’s protection, I... I fear I wouldn’t even be able to survive!"

Chen Sixuan instinctively retorted.

Gao Zhaoyu sighed softly and took Chen Sixuan’s hand. "Sixuan, you’re underestimating yourself. I’m not asking you to sever ties with your brother and sister-in-law, never to interact with them again. What I mean is, even without your brother’s protection, you can still live well."

She paused for a few seconds before sincerely adding, "Sixuan, you’re exceptionally skilled at embroidery. I’ve seen your work; your flowers, birds, fish, and insects are so lifelike that even my mother couldn’t stop praising them. Even the master artisans at the Jin Xiu Fang embroidery workshop might not match your skill. With such talent, why worry about not being able to support yourself?"

Chen Sixuan was stunned by her words and timidly countered, "But for a woman to go out in public to sell embroidery. Wouldn’t that invite criticism? Besides, the meager income from that... how could it be enough to live on? Not to mention, if my brother... if my brother finds out, he’ll throw me out of the house..."

"Criticism?" Gao Zhaoyu slightly raised her eyebrows. "It’s not the ancient times anymore. There are even female officials in the court now, so why can’t a woman earn her own living?"

Though she said this, she also understood that women like them, raised in privilege, had never supported themselves before, so their anxiety was natural.

"Sixuan, this is just a suggestion. Talking about it and doing it are different, so it’s only natural for you to feel uneasy."

Gao Zhaoyu lightly tapped the table with her fingers, her expression easing. "How about this: I’ll ask my mother to take you in as her adopted daughter. That way, you’ll be the dry daughter of a princess. If your brother tries to force you into marriage, he’ll have to think twice."

Chen Sixuan’s face lit up with hope, but then she grew worried again. "This... this would be too much trouble for you. What about my brother..."

"My mother has always liked you, so she shouldn’t refuse." Gao Zhaoyu said. "As for your brother, he’s the most pragmatic. Right now, though the Yongchang Marquis’s residence is facing some troubles, it’s still a marquis’s estate and related by marriage to the Prince of Wei’s residence. He can’t afford to offend them."

Chen Sixuan’s eyes filled with hope, blinking back tears. "Really... is that possible?"

Gao Zhaoyu smiled gently. "Don’t worry. I can’t just stand by and watch you jump into a fire pit."

"But this is only a temporary solution. Your... marriage still needs to be carefully considered. Don’t have any more conflicts with your brother when you go back. Wait for my news."

chapters.title: Clear Eyes
chapters.content:
After bidding farewell to Chen Sixuan, Gao Zhaoyu followed Cui Heng’s advice and went to Wenhua Pavilion to buy some paper and ink.

Upon returning to the Marquis’s estate, she went straight to Li Zhuangjin’s courtyard. At the entrance, she took a deep breath, suppressing the inexplicable flutter in her heart from her chance encounter with Cui Heng on the street.

Inside, Li Zhuangjin was sitting by the window reviewing account books. Seeing her enter, she looked up with a smile. “You’re back? What did you buy?”

“I bought some paper and ink at Wenhua Pavilion.” Gao Zhaoyu placed the items down and sat beside her mother. “Are you well today, Mother?”

Li Zhuangjin closed the ledger and rubbed her temples. “I’m fine. Just some trivial matters.”

Gao Zhaoyu felt slightly relieved and pondered how to bring up the idea of adopting Chen Sixuan as a sworn daughter.

“Mother,” before she could figure out how to mention Chen Sixuan, she first thought of Cui Heng. “Today on the street, I ran into Cui Heng.”

Li Zhuangjin’s hands paused, and she looked up at her. “Cui Heng?”

“Mm.” Gao Zhaoyu nodded, appearing indifferent. “Outside Moyun Study, my hairpin fell, and he helped me pick it up.”

She briefly recounted the encounter, omitting the part where she had asked for his name, only mentioning that he had introduced himself.

Li Zhuangjin listened silently, her eyes flickering with complex emotions. After Gao Zhaoyu finished, she sighed softly and took her daughter’s hand in hers.

“Zhaoyu, since you’ve brought it up, your mother won’t hide it from you.” Li Zhuangjin’s expression turned serious. “A few days ago, when I entered the palace, Her Majesty the Empress mentioned your marriage to Cui Heng again.”

Gao Zhaoyu’s heart skipped a beat, but her face remained composed, feigning confusion.

“Her Majesty’s meaning is that, given the current timing, settling this marriage would benefit both the Gao and Cui families.”

Li Zhuangjin’s expression was calm, but the faint furrow between her brows betrayed her inner unease.

“Minister Xu is pressing hard, sigh… it’s all such a mess. If the Gao and Cui families can use this opportunity to renew their old friendship, His Majesty might show leniency.”

Gao Zhaoyu pressed her lips together. “What does Mother think?”

“I…” Li Zhuangjin hesitated, her eyes filling with tenderness. “Zhaoyu, your mother doesn’t want to force you. Though this marriage is a good match, if you are unwilling, your mother will risk her reputation to refuse Her Majesty.”

Gao Zhaoyu lifted her gaze to the faint white strands at her mother’s temples. These days, her mother had been burdened with so many worries for the family. She thought of her father’s sighs in the study, of Wen Zhu and her brother far away in Xuzhou, of the troubles caused by the second branch of the family…

This family could not afford any more chaos.

“Mother,” she spoke softly, her voice steady. “Your daughter is willing.”

Li Zhuangjin blinked. “You… truly? Once you agree, there’s no turning back.”

Gao Zhaoyu nodded, a gentle smile lifting the corners of her lips. “I have long heard of the First Young Master Cui’s character and talents. Today, upon seeing him… he is indeed as the rumors say, a true gentleman. To marry him would be my fortune.”

Li Zhuangjin looked at her, tears welling in her eyes.

“Good child…” Li Zhuangjin pulled her daughter into her arms, her voice choked with emotion.

Gao Zhaoyu leaned against her mother’s shoulder, but the indifference she had felt the last time her mother mentioned this marriage was gone.

Mother and daughter embraced for a moment before Li Zhuangjin released her, wiping her eyes. “Since you’re willing, I’ll send a request to enter the palace tomorrow and give Her Majesty my answer. Now that the marriage is settled, we should start preparing. Cui Heng is not young, and the Cui family likely wishes for an early wedding.”

“As Mother arranges.”

Gao Zhaoyu nodded lightly, but suddenly wondered. Did Cui Heng know her? If not, had he already agreed to this marriage?

Did Cui Heng recognize her? Had he known who she was on the street today?

Li Zhuangjin noticed Gao Zhaoyu’s absentmindedness and gently shook her arm. “Zhaoyu, what are you thinking about?”

Gao Zhaoyu snapped back to reality, laughing it off with a vague response.

Li Zhuangjin pondered for a moment. “With so much happening in the family, the wedding shouldn’t be too extravagant, but it can’t be too modest either; it wouldn’t do you justice. In my opinion, we should set the date for autumn. By then, the storms should have passed, and it will be the perfect season.”

“Autumn…” Gao Zhaoyu repeated softly, a vague sense of melancholy rising in her heart.

“Mother, is it true what Minister Xu said about Father… that he accepted bribes and abused his power?”

Li Zhuangjin looked at Gao Zhaoyu’s burning gaze in surprise, her expression cooling.

“Your father’s matters are none of your concern.”

Seeing that Gao Zhaoyu still wanted to press, Li Zhuangjin changed the subject.

“Oh, I heard from your maid that the Chen family’s girl invited you to meet today?”

Gao Zhaoyu saw that her mother was unwilling to answer, and her own heart already had its answer; a sourness like unripe plums, a bitterness like rhubarb.

She collected herself and recounted Chen Sixuan’s predicament, then said, “Your daughter wishes to ask Mother for a favor. Could we take Sixuan as a sworn daughter? Her brother is forcing her to marry Staff Officer Liu as his second wife. That Liu Mingcheng is nearly forty, with a house full of children. If Sixuan marries him, her life will be ruined.”

Li Zhuangjin frowned. “That Chen boy is so foolish!”

She had a favorable impression of Chen Sixuan; gentle, quiet, and exceptionally skilled in needlework. As for Liu Mingcheng, she knew of him. Though his official rank was decent, he was far too slick and worldly. His first wife’s death had been under suspicious circumstances…

“We’ll help.” Li Zhuangjin decided immediately. “Tomorrow, I’ll send word to the Chen family to take Sixuan as my sworn daughter. With the Marquis of Yongchang’s backing, Chen Mingde won’t dare cause trouble.”

Gao Zhaoyu’s heart eased. “Thank you, Mother.”

“No need for thanks.” Li Zhuangjin patted her hand. “That child is pitiful. We’ll help where we can. But…”

She paused, looking at her daughter. “Zhaoyu, you can help Sixuan, but your own marriage is something you must walk through yourself. Though Cui Heng is a good man, the Cui family is complex. After you marry into it, you must be cautious in every step.”

Gao Zhaoyu forced a smile. “Your daughter understands.”

“Good that you understand.” Li Zhuangjin sighed. “Go on, you must be tired from going out. Rest early. The affairs of the Marquis’s estate are not your concern.”

Gao Zhaoyu obeyed and took her leave.

As she stepped out of Li Zhuangjin’s courtyard, the sky had already darkened. Lanterns along the corridor lit up one by one, casting a warm, golden glow on the bluestone path.

Gao Zhaoyu walked slowly, her mind once again filled with the image of those calm, deep eyes.

Cui Heng.

She silently repeated his name, her heart a mix of emotions.

Then she gave a self-deprecating laugh. The past was too painful to recall. Why dwell on it and ruin the future?

Qing Dai, holding a lantern, walked beside her. “Miss, do you truly wish to marry First Young Master Cui?”

Gao Zhaoyu stopped, her gloomy mood inexplicably lifting.

“Why not?” She chuckled softly, lightly tapping Qing Dai’s forehead. “You saw him today too. He’s handsome, has a pleasant voice, and is talented. In every way, he’s better than that heartless Cui Yao.”

Qing Dai gasped, scolding Gao Zhaoyu for being improper. Choosing a husband was about character, not superficial things. She warned her mistress not to judge a book by its cover.

This amused Gao Zhaoyu, and she covered her mouth, laughing. “Oh, come now, it’s all about fate. I wanted to connect with Cui Yao, but he never gave me the chance.”

Qing Dai immediately agreed, launching into a tirade against Cui Yao.

“Oh, Miss! Ever since that Cui Yao was beaten by the First Young Master while wearing a sack, he’s disappeared from the social circles in the capital! There’s been no news of him for two months. Maybe…”

Qing Dai’s voice was laced with malicious speculation, her face alight with gossip.

Gao Zhaoyu shook her head, smiling. “No, he wouldn’t be. If his legs were really broken, the Cui family would have come knocking on our door long ago. Probably just superficial injuries. My brother wouldn’t hit that hard.”

Qing Dai sighed in disappointment, then cursed Cui Yao a few more times before the two continued through the corridor toward Gao Zhaoyu’s courtyard.

Meanwhile, in the Cui estate, Cui Heng stood by the window of his study, gazing at the same moon, toying with a white jade hairpin in his hand.

It was identical to the one he had picked up from her hair that day.

The hairpin was smooth and cool to the touch.

Cui Heng played with it, recalling the girl’s flushed cheeks as she took it back, her forced composure, and the clear, bright eyes with which she had asked his name…

“Gao Zhaoyu.”

He softly spoke her name, a smile tugging at his lips.

After seeing her today, he suddenly felt that perhaps… this wasn’t entirely a miscalculation.

---

chapters.title: A Perfect Match
chapters.content:
Madame Cui, holding a teacup, looked at her grandson sitting upright before her, her eyes brimming with affection and satisfaction.

Ten years had passed, and the once silent and reserved boy had grown into such a steady and composed young man, exuding noble bearing and grace. Every movement was the epitome of a scion from a distinguished family.

“Heng,” Madame Cui set down her teacup and spoke gently, “you are twenty-seven this year, are you not?”

Cui Heng’s lips curved into a warm smile as he gave a slight bow. “Yes, Grandmother.”

“Being away for ten years, busy with official duties, you’ve had no time to attend to your own matters.”

Madame Cui sighed, her eyes filled with concern. “I know you have great ambitions, but establishing a family comes first. Now that you’ve returned to the capital, your marriage… should be put on the agenda.”

Cui Heng’s expression remained unchanged, still as gentle as jade. “This grandson understands. I’ve caused you worry, Grandmother.”

His compliance put Madame Cui at ease, and her tone grew even softer. “Over the years, many in the capital have been anxious about your marriage. Matchmakers have nearly worn out our doorstep. Your mother… Lin Shi has also looked at many families for you, but with you so far away in Xuzhou, it was never convenient.”

She paused, observing her grandson’s reaction. Seeing that he merely listened with a smile, she felt reassured and continued, “Now that you’re back, some things should be settled. I know you have your own judgment, but for a lifelong matter, your elders must consider it carefully for you.”

“Grandmother is right.” Cui Heng gave a slight nod, his voice gentle. “This grandson has been away for years and knows little of the young ladies in the capital. I will leave it entirely to Grandmother, Father, and Mother to decide.”

His respectful words pleased Madame Cui, though she secretly sighed at how overly composed her grandson was.

She smiled affectionately and slowly said, “Do you still remember your Qin family cousin? When you were little, you even said you would marry her when you grew up.”

Madame Cui spoke lightly, as if it were true.

Cui Heng merely smiled and nodded. “Ah, so it was the Qin family’s young lady.”

“That Ruochun girl from the Qin family is now in the prime of her youth. Last year, when she came to pay New Year’s respects, she had grown even more radiant.”

Madame Cui sighed. “That child is dignified, virtuous, and exceptionally talented. She has a fine reputation in Yongzhou. I was curious why she hasn’t found a match yet, only to learn that she has a heart set solely on you.”

Cui Heng chuckled softly. “Then I have let Young Lady Ruochun down.”

Madame Cui’s heart leapt with joy at his response. “The Qin family may not be as illustrious as before, but they are still a noble and upright family. If Ruochun has set her heart on you, and you have the same intention, this grandmother would die without regret.”

“Grandmother, please don’t speak of such things. You must live a long life to see the future of the Cui family.”

Cui Heng’s brows furrowed slightly, his voice filled with filial piety.

Madame Cui’s initial unease melted away at his words.

“Of course, aside from Ruochun, there are a few other young ladies from good families. The youngest daughter of the Duke of Anguo, the niece of the Left Prime Minister; all are from distinguished families with excellent appearances. But none are as familiar or as emotionally connected to you…”

Cui Heng lowered his gaze, his long fingers lightly tracing the rim of the teacup. After a long moment, he looked up at Madame Cui, his eyes still holding that gentle, calm smile.

“Grandmother has considered everything. This grandson is ashamed.” His voice was clear and measured. “For my marriage, I will leave it entirely to you, Father, and Mother to decide.”

“The Cui family is already a target for many. If we marry a young lady from too prominent a family, it may invite trouble from those with ill intentions. The Qin family has a clean and upright reputation. This grandson has always respected them.”

“Good, good child.”

Madame Cui’s eyes welled with tears as she took Cui Heng’s hand. “If you think this way, then I am at ease. A month ago, I wrote to your Qin family uncle. I expect Ruochun will arrive in a few days. You two have a bond from childhood; when the time comes, help your grandmother entertain her properly.”

“Thank you, Grandmother, for your care.”

Cui Heng replied warmly, then turned his hand to gently hold Madame Cui’s aged hand. “This grandson has been unfilial, causing you so much worry. In the future, I will strive to bring honor to the family and live up to your and Father’s expectations.”

“You… have always been the most understanding.” Madame Cui patted the back of his hand, her affection overflowing. “I don’t ask for you to be greatly illustrious, only that you live safely and smoothly, find a good match, and have children.”

“This grandson will remember.”

Cui Heng smiled and agreed, then stayed to share some interesting stories from Xuzhou, his witty remarks drawing continuous laughter from Madame Cui.

It was not until night fell that Madame Cui finally let him leave.

Watching Cui Heng’s tall and straight figure disappear beyond the door, Madame Cui’s smile faded, and she remained silent for a long time.

A trusted maid standing beside her chuckled softly. “Madame, you can rest easy now. The First Young Master has such bearing and insight; truly one in a million.”

Madame Cui slowly nodded, her eyes filled with satisfaction. “He’s smarter and more sensible than Cui Yao. A good child.”

“An opportunity has been given. If the Qin family doesn’t seize it, they’ll have no one to blame but themselves for not appreciating your concern for your maiden family.”

The trusted maid massaged Madame Cui’s shoulders and laughed. “Don’t worry, Madame. You saw Young Lady Ruochun last year; she’s a clever girl. If it weren’t for that Second Young Master’s lack of appreciation, you’d be holding your great-grandchild by now!”

Madame Cui let out a cold snort, a flicker of anger crossing her face. “That good-for-nothing! His mother and he look down on the Qin family’s status, and I wouldn’t even want to marry Ruochun to that playboy!”

“Now it’s perfect. It aligns with Lin Shi and Cui Yao’s wishes; they want to marry that helpless Gao Yao Jia.” A mocking glint appeared in her eyes. “And they still dare to covet the position of head of the Cui family.”

She paused, her words heavy with meaning. “This is for the best. A perfect match, as it should be.”

chapters.title: Imperial Bestowal of Marriage
chapters.content:
On the auspicious day of the fifth day of the fifth month, the imperial procession bearing the decree arrived almost simultaneously at the Duke of Yongchang’s residence and the Cui residence.

The Duke of Yongchang’s residence had received prior notice, so the incense table in the main hall had long been prepared.

Gao Jun and Li Zhuangjin knelt at the front, their expressions seemingly calm. Yet, upon hearing the words "imperial bestowal of marriage," they couldn’t help but exhale in relief, as if a heavy burden had been lifted.

Gao Zhaoyu knelt beside her mother, her head slightly lowered. As the eunuch clearly recited the decree, with phrases like "a match made in heaven" and "a perfect couple destined by fate," the corners of her lips involuntarily curled up in the faintest smile.

The curve was subtle, yet it genuinely brightened her eyes.

The gentle figure she had encountered in the marketplace that day, and the name in the decree, overlapped in her mind, quietly dispelling the last trace of resentment and grievance in her heart.

In the corner of the hall, Gao Yao Jia and Zhao Shi, who had also been summoned to hear the decree, had their eyes light up with intense joy upon hearing that "Cui Heng" and "Gao Zhaoyu" were to be wed by imperial decree.

Zhao Shi was so overwhelmed with emotion that she nearly collapsed, only managing to stay on her knees by holding onto her daughter.

How could they not be joyful?

The great ship of the Gao family had been tossed by storms and waves for so long, and now it had finally caught sight of the dawn of safe harbor.

His Majesty personally bestowing the marriage between the Cui and Gao families, with the eldest son Cui Heng; the orphan of the Grand Princess, who was most favored by the Emperor; was clearly a signal of imperial protection.

As long as the Gao family remained unharmed, their branch would have a chance to survive. Gao Yao Jia’s marriage, which had to be kept as low-key as possible, could now proceed smoothly.

All jealousy and resentment paled in comparison to the survival of the family and their own safety.

Gao Yao Jia even felt that the decree had come at the perfect time. The higher her eldest sister married, the more stable the Gao family would be, and perhaps her future days in the Cui family could be a little easier thanks to this connection.

"Your subjects (this humble wife, this commoner) accept the decree and express gratitude. Long live the Emperor, long live the Emperor, long may he reign!"

Gao Jun took the bright yellow scroll. The heavy stone in his heart finally settled, sweeping away the gloom of past days. His eyes grew slightly moist as he looked at Li Zhuangjin. Supporting his wife to rise, he gazed at his daughter with a mixture of relief and affection.

This decree not only gave Zhaoyu a future far beyond what she had before but also ensured the survival of the Gao family. Otherwise, he didn’t know how he would have answered to his ancestors in the future.
