After seeing off the imperial messengers, the atmosphere in the hall was completely different from the heavy oppression of the past few days. Though the servants did not dare to be noisy, their eyes and expressions carried a hint of joy.

Gao Zhaoyu held the decree and bowed deeply to her parents. "Daughter has caused Father and Mother much worry."

Li Zhuangjin stepped forward, took her hand, and gently patted it. "Good child, your blessings lie ahead."

Her gaze swept over Zhao Shi and her daughter, who seemed to want to speak but hesitated. She paused, her tone softening. "Second sister-in-law, though Wenju’s coming-of-age ceremony was disrupted, now that His Majesty has bestowed this marriage, and Zhaoyu has found such a good match, it is a blessing for our Gao family.

Yao Jia’s marriage can also be prepared. After all, they are sisters. In the future, within the Cui family, they must look out for each other."

Zhao Shi, as if pardoned from a great crime, quickly pulled Gao Yao Jia forward, her face beaming with smiles, her words filled with deference and enthusiasm. "Eldest sister-in-law is right! This is a tremendous joy! Congratulations to eldest sister-in-law, congratulations to the Duke, congratulations to Zhaoyu! Jia’er, why don’t you quickly congratulate your eldest sister!"

At this moment, Gao Yao Jia’s resentment had completely dissipated. Marrying Cui Yan and continuing to live well would certainly be better than her current situation.

With this thought, she sincerely bowed to Gao Zhaoyu, her voice carrying a touch of ingratiation. "Congratulations, eldest sister! Eldest sister, this is a great joy!"

Gao Zhaoyu gave a slight nod, accepting her greeting. With a smile, she let the past grievances slide, feeling only that the ways of the world were wondrous.

---

The atmosphere in the main hall of the Cui residence was far from as "joyous" as that of the Duke of Yongchang’s residence.

This marriage had come suddenly, and the Cui family was completely unprepared.

It was only when they heard that the imperial messengers had arrived at the gate that Cui Yan hastily led the entire household to receive the decree, his heart inexplicably skipping a beat.

When he heard the names "Cui Heng" and "Gao Zhaoyu" being tightly linked together, sanctioned by royal authority as husband and wife, his brows furrowed sharply before quickly smoothing out as he kowtowed in gratitude.

The Emperor’s will was absolute, bypassing all the usual steps of betrothal negotiations and formal inquiries, settling the matter with a single stroke.

Weighing the pros and cons in his mind, he finally let out a silent sigh; His Majesty intended to use Cui Heng to thoroughly bind the Gao family and the ambiguous relationship with the Prince of Wei.

Cui Old Madam knelt perfectly straight, but the prayer beads in her hands had stopped moving. The contents of the decree were like a block of ice, dropped into the carefully calculated lake of her heart.

Qin Ruochun... her niece by marriage, whom her maiden family had painstakingly cultivated, and whom she had planned to use to tie down Cui Heng, strengthening the connection between her maiden family and the Cui family, had not even arrived in the capital. All her plans had turned to dust before this golden, shining decree.

For the first time, the usually kind and benevolent smile on her face seemed a little stiff, and her voice of gratitude carried a hint of dryness.

Disappointment and frustration at the disruption of her plans churned within her, yet she could not reveal the slightest hint of it. She had to feign joy: "His Majesty’s great favor... Heng’er obtaining such a fine match is this old one’s blessing."

Lin Xueyan lowered her head, but the corners of her mouth almost couldn’t help but lift.

Imperial bestowal of marriage? Her haughty mother-in-law had always wanted to push that Qin Ruochun from her maiden family onto Cui Yan, hadn’t she? When Cui Yan refused, she set her sights on Cui Heng.

Now, with the Emperor’s decree, let’s see how she would manage! Watching her mother-in-law’s plans fall through gave Lin Xueyan a satisfaction as refreshing as drinking iced water on the hottest day of summer.

As for whom Cui Heng married, well, it wasn’t her own son. As long as it didn’t affect Cui Yan, she was more than happy to see it happen.

Thus, her voice of gratitude was particularly loud: "This humble wife thanks His Majesty for his great favor! Long live the Emperor’s wisdom!"

Cui Yan and Cui Yulan knelt at the end, their emotions too complex for words.

Cui Yulan lowered her eyes, her mind racing. With this, both of the Cui family’s legitimate sons would be married to daughters of the Gao family. Her grandmother would no longer try to marry her off to that brute, Gao Yuan.

A smile of joy tugged at her lips, but fearing that Cui Old Madam might notice, she quickly lowered her head again.

Among everyone present, only Cui Heng maintained a calm and composed expression from beginning to end.

He knelt gracefully, accepted the decree steadily, and his voice was clear and gentle: "This subject, Cui Heng, accepts the decree and expresses gratitude."

Cui Old Madam, her plans in ruins, could not find a single word to say.

Lin Xueyan, laughing so hard that her face seemed to blossom, as if the imperial bestowal had been for her own son, sincerely blessed Cui Heng and Gao Zhaoyu with a lifetime of happiness and harmony. She then pulled along the gloomy Cui Yan and the equally delighted Cui Yulan as she took her leave.

She needed to quickly find a noble family for her daughter, preferably settling the marriage before that old woman recovered her wits. Otherwise, she might try to use them again to elevate that hopeless Qin family.

As everyone dispersed with their own thoughts, Cui Yan coldly glanced at Cui Heng before finally saying, "The Emperor’s will is set. You had best prepare."

"I understand, Father," Cui Heng said with a slight bow. "His Majesty’s bestowal is a great favor to the Cui family. This son will naturally comply with the decree and handle matters properly."

Cui Yan swept out, his sleeves fluttering.

Cui Heng, however, paid it little mind. He continued to smile gently. But as he smiled, the corners of his mouth seemed to overflow with amusement.

chapters.title: Opening an Embroidery Workshop
chapters.content:
Chen Sixuan’s marriage finally fell through.

First, Li Zhuangjin had taken her as an adopted daughter, which greatly diminished her status. Second, the marriage between Cui Heng and Gao Zhaoyu was a royal decree. The next morning at court, the emperor dismissed all previous impeachments against the Cui and Gao families with a wave of his hand, offering only a verbal reprimand.

The Cui and Gao families once again became the "worthy ministers" and "loyal subjects" in the emperor’s eyes.

Seeing this, the court officials realized that the emperor had never intended to take action against the two families. Once this was clear, the Left Prime Minister also withdrew his nearly two-month-long suppression of the Right Prime Minister, Cui Yan, and smiled as he cupped his hands in congratulations.

Chen Sixuan’s brother, Chen Mingde, also rose in power. Even without Li Zhuangjin adopting his sister, he would never have allowed his sister to marry Liu Mingcheng.

"Zhaoyu, I want to open my own embroidery workshop," Chen Sixuan said firmly as she visited to express her gratitude. "My skills are decent, and over the years, I’ve secretly saved some money of my own. If… if you could help me a little, or perhaps… we could go into business together…"

Gao Zhaoyu was just trying on new jewelry in front of a mirror; prepared in advance by her mother for her upcoming marriage. Hearing this, she set down the red-gold-and-kingfisher-feather hairpiece in her hand, turned around, and her eyes were filled with delight.

"Sixuan, it’s wonderful that you thought of this."

She pulled Chen Sixuan down to sit beside her. "Opening an embroidery workshop is a great idea. Not only will it give you a foundation to rely on, but in the future, it might also help other women in similar situations."

Chen Sixuan’s eyes lit up. "You… you think it’s feasible?"

"Of course it is," Gao Zhaoyu replied without hesitation. "Don’t worry about the money; I’ll invest. But this matter requires careful planning. Choosing a location, hiring workers, connecting with clients… none of it is easy. Moreover, you are still an unmarried young lady from an official family. If you personally step forward to manage it, it might invite criticism."

"I’m not afraid of criticism," Chen Sixuan tightened her grip on her hands. "As long as I can avoid being at others’ mercy, I’m willing to try. As for management… I can hire a reliable shop manager first and mainly oversee the embroidery quality and designs from behind the scenes."

Gao Zhaoyu looked at the light in her eyes and felt a sense of comfort.

She pondered for a moment. "Alright, go back and carefully draft a plan. Figure out how much capital you need, where you want the shop to be, what kind of embroidery you’ll focus on; get a clear idea first. I’ll handle the money. As for your brother…"

She smiled slightly. "Since Mother has already taken you as her adopted daughter, you are now part of the Yongchang Marquis’s household. Whatever business you want to do, as long as it’s legal, he has no say in it. If he asks, just tell him it was my idea. If he’s not satisfied, let him come find me."

Chen Sixuan was so moved she didn’t know what to say. She could only tightly grasp Gao Zhaoyu’s hand and nod repeatedly.

After seeing Chen Sixuan off, Gao Zhaoyu felt a little lighter in spirit. She was happy to help her good friend find a way forward.

If Sixuan could open an embroidery workshop, maybe she could open a spice shop or a teahouse. That way, she’d have her own business too.

---

Cui Yan’s injuries were far more serious than anyone knew.

That day, Gao Yuan had struck him in a rage, deliberately targeting his weak points. With the help of a group of disgruntled noble sons who "lent a hand," Cui Yan had suffered two broken ribs, a cracked left leg, and internal injuries. When he returned home unconscious and covered in blood, it was no act.

The Cui family had hired the best physicians and used the most expensive medicines. After more than two months of care, his external wounds had healed, and he could walk again. But the internal damage and the hidden pain in his leg were not so easily resolved.

What was even harder for Cui Yan to bear was the psychological torment.

After finally enduring the boredom of bed rest, he faced the subtle alienation from his social circle in the capital. Even though the Cui family tried to cover it up, the rumors of what had happened at the Yongchang Marquis’s residence and his beating had still spread quietly.

The profligate young masters who had once called him brother and spent their days with him in cockfights and horse races now greeted him with awkwardness or outright avoidance.

Depressed, he shut himself indoors, even taking leave from his duties at the Ministry of Justice.

Every day, as he lay in bed, he couldn’t help but think of how, before long, Gao Yao Jia would be carried into the house in a small sedan chair through the side gate. The thought made his internal organs feel as if they were burning.

He had smashed countless teacups and porcelain in his rage.

Cui Heng’s return completely shattered his last line of defense.

He locked himself in his room, smashed countless teacups and porcelain, roared at Lin Xueyan’s attempts to comfort him, and ignored Cui Yan’s reprimands from outside the door.

Lin Xueyan watched her son grow darker day by day, her heart filled with anxiety.

She tried to comfort him with words like "there’s still time," "wait for your father to secure a good position for you," and "once Gao Yao Jia enters the house, you can control her." But this only provoked greater fury from Cui Yan.

Now, even Lin Xueyan rarely went to check on him, only ordering the servants to take good care of him while she turned a blind eye to avoid further anger.

Finally, on a bright spring day, Cui Yan, leaning on a crutch, slowly walked in the garden to clear his mind. From a distance, he saw Cui Heng accompanying the old madam Cui in the lakeside pavilion, deep in conversation.

Under the warm spring sun, the grandmother and grandson chatted and laughed, the wrinkles on the old madam’s face smoothing out with affection. Cui Heng listened attentively, occasionally nodding, his manner respectful and gentle. The harmonious scene was almost blinding.

Cui Yan gripped his crutch tightly, his knuckles turning white.

A surge of malicious anger rushed to his head. He suddenly let out a cold laugh, turned around, and limped away.

Cui Heng, with a smile on his face, caught a glimpse of Cui Yan’s furious retreating figure from the corner of his eye. His smile only deepened.

The old madam Cui was enthusiastically discussing the recent movements of her niece from the Qin family, Qin Ruochun, in the capital. Her words carried no small amount of regret and probing.

"That child Ruochun is so knowledgeable and accomplished. Even her painting skills are top-notch among the capital’s young ladies… Just a few days ago, she sent me a hand-painted Pine Cranes of Longevity through someone. Her brushwork has become even more refined."

The old madam sighed as she spoke, her regret evident.

Qin Ruochun had arrived in the capital three days ago but could only stay temporarily at an inn.

Cui Heng poured tea for his grandmother with a gentle smile. "Cousin Qin is indeed talented. I heard from Uncle Fu that she has been preparing a small poetry and painting gathering these past few days. Many talented women in the capital have received invitations."

A flicker of disappointment flashed in the old madam’s eyes, but she quickly smiled again. "Yes, that child always loves such things. Heng, now that you’ve returned to the capital, you should also socialize more with the young gentlemen of various families to rebuild your connections. Your brother is unreliable, so the future of the Cui family ultimately depends on you."

Cui Heng paused in his movement of stirring the tea, a hint of joy flashing in his eyes before he suppressed it.

"I understand. But with the wedding approaching, there are many matters to attend to, so I fear I won’t have time for that just yet. Once things settle down, I will naturally pay visits to the various uncles and elders."

The old madam nodded and said no more.

---

Back in his own courtyard, the resentment in Cui Yan’s chest grew thicker.

He looked at the luxurious yet hollow furnishings in his room, thought of the infuriating scene he had just witnessed in the garden, and then considered his current awkward position in the household and his tarnished reputation outside…

He couldn’t just let this go.

Wasn’t Cui Heng about to marry Gao Zhaoyu in grand style? Wasn’t he going to use this imperial-decreed marriage to climb even higher?

He would make sure they didn’t have it so easy.

Gao Zhaoyu… wasn’t she always dignified and virtuous, valuing her reputation? If, on the eve of the wedding, some damaging rumors about her were spread, even if they were just groundless, if it cast a shadow over this "match made in heaven" and embarrassed Cui Heng, he would feel much better.

Spreading rumors? Too crude, and easy to trace back. Manufacturing an "accidental" encounter to make it seem as if there was "lingering affection" between them? Too risky. Gao Zhaoyu might not cooperate, and Cui Heng was no easy opponent.

Cui Yan paced anxiously in his room, his gaze sweeping over the bookshelf and landing on a book about anecdotes and wild histories from the previous dynasty. A spark of inspiration struck him.

Didn’t Gao Zhaoyu love literature, chess, calligraphy, and painting, and often associate with scholars, artists, and close female friends?

If he could target someone close to her and weave a "story"…

For example, if Gao Zhaoyu couldn’t let go of an old love and had some "letter exchanges" or "private tutoring" with a certain "talented" scholar or painter, and this was "accidentally" discovered…

Then, Cui Heng would be humiliated, and he would finally feel satisfied.

This thought brought a twisted sense of pleasure to Cui Yan.

He immediately called for one of his more reliable long-term servants and took out a bag of silver.

"Go find someone; someone clever and tight-lipped. First, have them keep a close eye on the eldest lady of the Yongchang Marquis’s household and the people she frequently associates with. If there’s anything unusual, especially any contact with unfamiliar men, report to me immediately. Remember, do it discreetly."

The servant hesitated upon hearing this. "Second Young Master, if… if the Marquis and the Lady find out…"

"Just do as I say!" Cui Yan snapped. "If you do this well, you’ll be rewarded handsomely. If word gets out…" He gave the servant an icy look.

The servant shivered and dared not say more. He took the silver and hurried away.

Cui Yan walked to the window, looking out at the bright spring scenery, a cold smile curling at the corner of his mouth.

Gao Zhaoyu, Cui Heng; your good days won’t come so easily.

A storm brews from the slightest breeze, and this time, he would personally stir up this pool of muddy water.

The servant walked out the door, cursing under his breath as he looked back. He weighed the silver in his hand, his expression disdainful.

Did he think this little bit of silver was enough to buy his loyalty?

Without hesitation, he went straight to Cui Heng’s courtyard and reported Cui Yan’s "plan" to Cui Heng’s trusted aide. After receiving a large sum of silver, he left satisfied.

As for the task of watching Gao Zhaoyu, he had already forgotten about it.

At the Yongchang Marquis’s residence, Gao Zhaoyu was discussing with her mother, Li Zhuangjin, the idea of using her years of savings and some of the "liquid assets" from her dowry to manage a few stable businesses in the capital.

She didn’t seek huge profits, only a business she could control that would provide a steady income, like Chen Sixuan’s embroidery workshop.

"Opening a spice shop or a teahouse; both seem good. A spice shop requires little capital but offers steady profits. A teahouse, if it can gain a reputation for elegance, would also be a good place to network."

Gao Zhaoyu analyzed carefully. "What do you think, Mother?"

Li Zhuangjin pondered, pleased by her daughter’s foresight and independence. "It’s good that you have this in mind. But you’re about to be married, and the Cui family is of such high status. A new bride being too involved in business might invite gossip.

"Why not… do it in my name first, or have a reliable steward handle it openly while you manage things behind the scenes. Once you’re married and have established yourself, you can gradually take over."

Gao Zhaoyu knew her mother’s concerns were valid and nodded. "I understand. I’ll follow your advice."

Li Zhuangjin ordered a nanny to bring out a small box and placed it beside Gao Zhaoyu. "These are the deeds to some shops and properties in the capital. There’s a shop in the south with a good location. It used to be a silk business, but the owner returned to his hometown half a year ago, so it’s been vacant since. If you want to open a spice shop, that place would be just the right size."

Gao Zhaoyu took the box and opened it. Inside were not only the property deeds but also account books for more than a dozen farms and tea plantations in the south.

Her eyes welled up with tears; these were clearly Li Zhuangjin’s personal assets. "Mother…"

"Silly child, you’re my daughter. Of course I have to think more for you." She patted Gao Zhaoyu’s hand. "Go ahead and do it. These shops, farms, and tea plantations are all under my personal management. Even the Marquis’s household doesn’t know about them."

"Your dowry includes hundreds of properties and lands, but they’re all out in the open. If you want to engage in private transactions, it’s inconvenient."

"Thank you, Mother." Gao Zhaoyu’s nose tingled as she tightly gripped her mother’s hand in return.

chapters.title: Stubborn as a Mule
chapters.content:
However, Gao Zhaoyu did not take Li Zhuangjin’s advice to open a spice shop on South Street.

Although Chen Sixuan had saved some private funds, it was far from enough to open a shop.

Gao Zhaoyu was still undecided between opening a spice shop or a teahouse, so she simply rented the shop to Chen Sixuan.

Chen Sixuan tightly gripped her hand, her throat choked with emotion, unable to speak.

Finding a suitable shop was no easy task, and then there was the deposit; she had been so worried about this that she couldn’t eat or sleep.

"Zhaoyu, thank you... I will never forget your kindness for the rest of my life..."

Gao Zhaoyu was most afraid of seeing others cry and didn’t know how to comfort her, so she forced a lighthearted joke: "Don’t get too happy too soon. If you use my shop, you’ll not only have to pay rent but also give me a share of the profits."

Chen Sixuan wiped her tears and laughed through them: "Understood, Miss Gao! If I don’t make money, you’ll have to bear the losses yourself!"

Gao Zhaoyu pretended to ponder: "Hmm... in that case, won’t I be at a loss?"

The two chatted and laughed, and finally settled on the name for the embroidery shop: Qiyun Embroidery Workshop.

After scraping together a large sum of money as startup capital, the preparations for the embroidery shop were complete.

The signboard for Qiyun Embroidery Workshop was modestly hung above the empty shop on South Street.

The storefront was small but elegantly arranged, clean and refined. As soon as one entered, the faint scent of sandalwood and the unique aroma of silk threads filled the air.

With Gao Zhaoyu’s help, Chen Sixuan hired a female manager who had once worked at a large embroidery workshop in Jiangnan. The manager, surnamed Su, was in her thirties, efficient and capable. The embroidery maidens were mostly women from respectable families who had signed labor contracts or widows with skills.

On the opening day, Gao Zhaoyu, wearing a veil hat, watched from a private room on the second floor of the teahouse across the street with Chen Sixuan.

There were no firecrackers or crowds of guests. Only Manager Su, along with two clever maids, displayed several exquisitely embroidered sample screens, handkerchiefs, and fan cases at the entrance.

Each embroidery piece was exquisite, especially a double-sided embroidery of Yutang Chun with different colors on each side, which attracted many ladies and young misses passing by to stop and admire.

"Zhaoyu, look..."

Chen Sixuan nervously twisted her handkerchief. Only when she saw someone inquiring about prices and buying a few small embroidery pieces did she let out a soft sigh, her eyes slightly red. "Someone actually bought them."

Gao Zhaoyu took her hand and smiled: "This is just the beginning. I trust your craftsmanship. Manager Su is also capable. Take it slow; once word of mouth spreads, business will improve."

The money she invested came from the private allowance her mother secretly gave her, not from the Hou府’s public funds. When Li Zhuangjin found out, he only smiled, tapped her forehead, and called her "quick-witted."

As Gao Zhaoyu had expected, business at the embroidery workshop gradually improved.

Chen Sixuan’s embroidery designs were novel and elegant, with exquisite materials and craftsmanship. Soon, the workshop gained a reputation among the wives and daughters of officials.

She spent most of her days in the quiet room at the back of the embroidery workshop, either guiding the embroidery maidens or burying herself in designing new patterns. She seemed to have found new hope, her face glowing, no longer the worried and gloomy look of the past.

The emperor’s decree put a definitive end to the turmoil between the Cui and Gao families.

In the imperial court, the civil and military officials understood the unspoken message.

Minister Xu’s petition to retire was left pending. After he repeatedly claimed illness to avoid court, the emperor finally, though reluctantly, granted his request to return home with his family in honor.

Meanwhile, the position of Minister of Personnel was quickly filled by the younger brother of Empress Xiao, a move that demonstrated the emperor’s favor; both thunder and rain were bestowed by imperial grace.

The new Minister of Personnel was from the same school as the Left Chancellor, leading many to speculate whether the emperor intended to balance the power of the Right Chancellor. But since the new minister was the empress’s brother, did that mean the Xiao family was siding with the Left Chancellor? Was this the emperor’s intention?

Hidden rifts and schemes silently grew.

Cui Heng, the emperor’s nephew who had been at the center of the power struggle since arriving in the capital, calmly requested a transfer from the Ministry of Personnel to the Ministry of Justice, where he was appointed Right Assistant Minister, a third-rank official.

The Minister of Justice, having witnessed the fate of the former Minister of Personnel, speculated that Cui Heng’s transfer without a prestigious title from the top ministry to the Ministry of Justice was likely the emperor’s way of "reminding" him. Thus, he hastily relinquished power.

Faced with Cui Heng’s impartial and fair demeanor in public, but his silent disregard for the cases he intended to investigate behind the scenes, the minister feigned ignorance, as if he knew nothing.

Sure enough, every time they met, the minister greeted Cui Heng with a warm smile.

Cui Heng’s heart rejoiced; he had indeed interpreted the emperor’s intentions correctly.

His official hat was safe.

"Assistant Minister Cui, wait…"

Ning Fu, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, hurriedly caught up with Cui Heng, who was leaving the office to return home.

"Assistant Minister…" he panted, out of breath from running a few steps, clutching his chest.

Cui Heng stopped, his expression indifferent. "What is it?"

Ning Fu finally caught his breath, fearing Cui Heng would leave again as he had before. He quickly said, "Assistant Minister, forgive me. It’s not that I didn’t want to let you leave, but the Left Chancellor has been pressing hard…"

As he spoke, he wiped the sweat from his temples, feeling bitter inside.

If it weren’t for the damned Left Chancellor forcing him to deal with someone as formidable as Cui Heng, why would he be in this position?

The Left Chancellor’s intention was clearly to suppress Cui Heng’s momentum, yet he had to be the one to deliver this offensive message!

Cui Heng listened silently, his expression still blank. Only after Ning Fu finished did he speak slowly, his calm gaze fixed on him, making Ning Fu break out in a cold sweat again.

"In the Ministry of Justice, we handle cases based on law and evidence. Since the case has already been brought to trial, it must be thoroughly investigated. As for who is involved and whether to prioritize harmony..."

He paused, his tone unchanged, brushing off his sleeve as if removing nonexistent dust. "That is a matter for the Left Chancellor and His Majesty to consider, not for us officials to meddle in."

Ning Fu was left speechless, his face pale. He hastily bowed. "Yes, yes, Assistant Minister is right. It was my mistake! But the Left Chancellor..."

"Principal Clerk Ning."

Cui Heng interrupted him, his voice carrying a warning. "You only need to report back to the Left Chancellor that Cui Heng, as Assistant Minister of Justice, will uphold the law impartially and not fail the emperor’s trust. As for the case, it will be investigated as it should be. If there are any uncertainties, I will personally seek guidance from His Majesty and the Left Chancellor."

With that, he no longer looked at Ning Fu’s ashen face. Giving a slight nod, he turned and left.

Ning Fu stood in place, watching Cui Heng’s tall and straight figure disappear into the twilight, feeling his back drenched in cold sweat.

This Assistant Minister Cui was young, but his actions were so unyielding; like a wall that no oil or salt could penetrate. The Left Chancellor had tried to stop the investigation, but instead, it had provoked Cui Heng’s defiance. It seemed he had kicked an iron board.

Ning Fu made a bitter face, pondering how to report back to the Left Chancellor while regretting taking on this thankless task.

---

chapters.title: Evidence and Witnesses Are in My Hands
chapters.content:
Only after boarding the carriage did the indifference on Cui Heng’s face gradually fade.

He closed his eyes to rest, his fingertips lightly tapping his knee unconsciously.

"Go to Shangyi Tower."

Cui Heng suddenly ordered.

The coachman outside immediately turned the carriage toward Shangyi Tower.

Shangyi Tower was located in the middle of South Street, separated from the newly opened Qiyun Embroidery Workshop across the street by a narrow road.

The teahouse had once been somewhat famous in the capital, but in recent years, due to poor management and a series of minor scandals, its business had declined, and it was on the verge of closing down.

In a quiet private room on the second floor of the teahouse, Left Chancellor Zheng Huai’an was unceremoniously lounging on a soft couch by the window, holding a plate of freshly stir-fried melon seeds, cracking them with relish, the shells scattered all over the floor.

In his early forties, slightly plump, with a round face, he looked very amiable. If not for the purple official robe symbolizing his high rank, he would have looked more like a wealthy, idle master.

"Master Brother, could you make some noise when you enter?"

Hearing the door push open, Zheng Huai’an didn’t even lift his head, lazily saying, "You scared me. I almost choked on a melon seed."

Though he said this, his hand remained steady as he tossed another seed into his mouth.

Cui Heng closed the door behind him with his other hand, long used to his senior brother’s antics.

He walked straight to the opposite seat, poured himself a cup of tea, and said calmly, "If a little noise could scare you to death, our teacher would have to crawl out of his grave to clean up his own school."

"Tsk, still so unlovable."

Zheng Huai’an finally spared him a glance, "I heard you made that old fox Ning Fu turn pale? Young man, don’t be so quick-tempered!"

"He’s just a messenger."

Cui Heng took a sip of tea. "The more strongly they react, the more anxious the people behind them will become. Didn’t you ask me to be a little ‘reckless’? I’m just following orders."

Zheng Huai’an grinned, sitting up a bit, brushing the debris from his hands. "I was anxious too. I’ve been waiting for you here for days, and you didn’t show up. What else could I do but send someone to deliver a message?"

"Those old men have been too comfortable for too long. Someone has to stir the hornet’s nest. But," he shifted the topic, narrowing his eyes slightly, "you’re fixated on the Liu case. Are you really planning to use the Right Chancellor’s disciple to tear open a gap? Don’t forget about your old man’s side..."

"The case is real. The evidence and witnesses are in my hands."

Cui Heng interrupted him, his expression calm. "As for whether it’s a warning shot or a full attack, it depends on His Majesty’s intentions and how high they jump. My transfer to the Ministry of Justice means investigating cases is my duty. As for whom you want to cut with this ‘knife’ of mine and how deep, that’s your call."

"Does that sound like something a person would say?"

Zheng Huai’an feigned distress, "We’re from the same school. You make it sound like I’m some scheming mastermind."

He grabbed a handful of melon seeds and leaned back again. "But as long as you know what you’re doing. That old fox Cui Yan is cunning. Be careful not to capsize in a gutter and waste all my effort in bringing you back from Xuzhou."

"No need to worry."

Cui Heng responded, about to discuss business, when his gaze casually fell out the window, landing directly on the entrance of Qiyun Embroidery Workshop across the street.

The shop door was open, revealing a glimpse of its elegant interior.

Suddenly, a familiar slender figure emerged from the embroidery workshop, lifting her veil hat, and met his gaze directly.

He smiled gently, slowly closing the window.

The girl’s poised figure was unmistakably Gao Zhaoyu.

Business at Qiyun Embroidery Workshop was improving, and she had been planning to open a spice or tea shop nearby to keep an eye on Chen Sixuan’s business.

Chen Sixuan spent almost every day at the embroidery workshop and was very familiar with the shops on this street. She wrote to Gao Zhaoyu, saying that the business at Shangyi Tower across the street was not doing well, and its closure was only a matter of time.

After reading the letter, Gao Zhaoyu went to negotiate with the manager of the teahouse about buying the property, expecting the price to be reasonable.

However, the manager said the owner behind the scenes was not selling, and that the decision was not his to make. Gao Zhaoyu had no choice but to leave disappointed.

As she discussed with her maid how to persuade the other party, as if by some telepathy, she looked up and gazed toward Shangyi Tower.

Her eyes met his.

Zheng Huai’an followed his gaze and, though Cui Heng had quickly closed the window, recognized her in an instant. "Oh," he exclaimed.

"Isn’t that your future wife? What, did investigating a case lead you to your own family’s property across the street?"

His tone was teasing. "Or are you using public office for private gain, deliberately choosing this place to meet me just to steal a glance at her?"

Cui Heng withdrew his gaze, glancing at him. "Do you think everyone is as idle as you? That building is about to collapse. I’d rather spend my time reviving it than sitting here listening to you crack melon seeds."

"Hey, you little…"

Zheng Huai’an was about to retort when he saw Gao Zhaoyu, supported by her maid, walking straight toward Shangyi Tower.

He immediately grinned. "Look, she’s coming for your ‘legitimate business.’ Is she here to compete with her future husband for territory or to inspect your work?"

Cui Heng ignored his teasing. Through the crack in the window, he saw Gao Zhaoyu and her maid inquiring about the price and the deed.

His hearing was excellent. Despite the distance, he could still hear the manager sighing and Gao Zhaoyu’s soft voice inquiring about the owner.

"Seems like she’s serious."

Zheng Huai’an stroked his chin, this time with a more serious look. "This location is good. If the embroidery workshop across the street really takes off, it’ll bring in foot traffic. Opening a teahouse or another elegant shop here would be a good idea. Better than letting it die in your hands."

Cui Heng picked up his teacup, not responding, his gaze fixed on the composed figure negotiating below.

"However, Master Brother," Zheng Huai’an’s tone became serious, lowering his voice, "marrying her means openly aligning yourself with Prince Wei’s faction. The emperor is using this marriage to balance the factions now, but who knows what he’ll think in the future."

Cui Heng set down his teacup, his fingers unconsciously tracing the rim. Outside the window, Gao Zhaoyu had apparently reached an agreement with the manager, as she was taking out a silver note and handing it to the now-smiling manager.

The spring sunlight bathed her, as if gilding her with a soft glow.

Zheng Huai’an watched him for a few seconds, then suddenly grinned, returning to his lazy demeanor. "Alright, you’ve always had a mind of your own. Just remember to invite me to the wedding. I’ll give a gift as I see fit."

He grabbed a handful of melon seeds, cracking them as he prepared to leave. "But for now, let’s focus on our main business. The rat is startled; its tail is bound to show. As for the Liu case, I think we should stoke the fire a bit more..."

Cui Heng turned his head. The two locked eyes, and Zheng Huai’an laughed heartily before leaving.

Cui Heng lowered his gaze to sip his tea but only heard the door open, not close. His heart skipped a beat. He turned to look again, meeting Gao Zhaoyu’s eyes once more.
